back_answer: Mumbai, due to its large concentration of cotton textile mills.

subject: Social Science (KTBS State Syllabus)
front_prompt: Why is the iron and steel industry considered a basic or key industry?
back_answer: Because its products serve as raw materials for heavy and light engineering industries, machinery, construction, and defense equipment.

subject: Social Science (KTBS State Syllabus)
front_prompt: Name the public sector iron and steel plant located in Karnataka.
back_answer: Visvesvaraya Iron and Steel Limited (VISL) located at Bhadravathi.

subject: Social Science (KTBS State Syllabus)
front_prompt: Which state is the leading producer of sugar in India?

subject: Social Science (KTBS State Syllabus)

subject: Social Science (KTBS State Syllabus)
front_prompt: What are the major problems faced by rural areas in India?

front_prompt: What role do Self-Help Groups (SHGs) play in rural development?

front_prompt: Differentiate between institutional and non-institutional sources of rural credit.

subject: Social Science (KTBS State Syllabus)
front_prompt: What is rural employment generation, and why is it necessary?

subject: Social Science (KTBS State Syllabus)
front_prompt: What is the significance of cottage and small-scale industries in rural areas?

front_prompt: How does land reform contribute to rural development?

back_answer: If a line is drawn parallel to one side of a triangle to intersect the other two sides in distinct points, the other two sides are divided in the same ratio.

front_prompt: State the Converse of the Basic Proportionality Theorem.
back_answer: If a line divides any two sides of a triangle in the same ratio, then the line is parallel to the third side.

subject: Mathematics
front_prompt: What is the AAA (Angle-Angle) Similarity Criterion?
back_answer: If in two triangles, corresponding angles are equal, then their corresponding sides are in the same ratio (proportional) and hence the two triangles are similar.

subject: Mathematics
front_prompt: What is the SAS (Side-Angle-Side) Similarity Criterion?
back_answer: If one angle of a triangle is equal to one angle of the other triangle and the sides including these angles are proportional, then the two triangles are similar.

subject: Mathematics
front_prompt: What is the SSS (Side-Side-Side) Similarity Criterion?
back_answer: If in two triangles, sides of one triangle are proportional to (i.e., in the same ratio of) the sides of the other triangle, then their corresponding angles are equal and hence the two triangles are similar.

subject: Mathematics
front_prompt: State the theorem on the ratio of the areas of two similar triangles.

subject: Mathematics
front_prompt: State the Pythagoras Theorem.

subject: Mathematics
front_prompt: State the Converse of the Pythagoras Theorem.
back_answer: In a triangle, if the square of one side is equal to the sum of the squares of the other two sides, then the angle opposite the first side is a right angle.

subject: Mathematics
front_prompt: When are two polygons of the same number of sides said to be similar?

back_answer: 4 (HH, HT, TH, TT)

subject: Science (Physics, Chemistry, Biology)
front_prompt: Why should a magnesium ribbon be cleaned before burning in air?
back_answer: To remove the protective layer of basic magnesium carbonate formed on its surface due to reaction with moist air, ensuring smooth burning.

subject: Science (Physics, Chemistry, Biology)
front_prompt: State any two observations that indicate a chemical reaction has taken place.
back_answer: Change in state, evolution of a gas, change in color, or change in temperature.

subject: Science (Physics, Chemistry, Biology)
front_prompt: What is a skeletal chemical equation?
back_answer: An unbalanced chemical equation that represents a chemical reaction using symbols and formulas without equal numbers of atoms of each element on both sides.

subject: Science (Physics, Chemistry, Biology)
front_prompt: Why is it important to balance a chemical equation?
back_answer: To satisfy the Law of Conservation of Mass, which states that mass can neither be created nor destroyed in a chemical reaction.

subject: Science (Physics, Chemistry, Biology)
front_prompt: Define a combination reaction with an example.
back_answer: A reaction in which two or more reactants combine to form a single product. Example: C(s) + O2(g) -> CO2(g).

subject: Science (Physics, Chemistry, Biology)
front_prompt: What is the difference between endothermic and exothermic reactions?
back_answer: Exothermic reactions release heat energy into the surroundings, whereas endothermic reactions absorb heat energy from the surroundings.

subject: Science (Physics, Chemistry, Biology)
front_prompt: What is observed when ferrous sulphate crystals are heated strongly?
back_answer: The green color of the crystals changes to white/brownish-black due to the formation of ferric oxide, and the characteristic smell of burning sulphur is evolved.

subject: Science (Physics, Chemistry, Biology)
front_prompt: Write the chemical equation for the displacement reaction between iron nails and copper sulphate solution.
back_answer: Fe(s) + CuSO4(aq) -> FeSO4(aq) + Cu(s)

subject: Science (Physics, Chemistry, Biology)
front_prompt: Define precipitation reaction and give an example.
back_answer: A reaction in which an insoluble substance (precipitate) is formed. Example: Na2SO4(aq) + BaCl2(aq) -> BaSO4(s) + 2NaCl(aq).

subject: Science (Physics, Chemistry, Biology)
front_prompt: What are the two common effects of oxidation reactions experienced in everyday life?
back_answer: Corrosion (e.g., rusting of iron) and Rancidity (oxidation of fats and oils in food leading to foul smell and taste).

subject: Science (Physics, Chemistry, Biology)
front_prompt: What is the chemical name and formula of washing soda?
back_answer: Sodium carbonate decahydrate, Na2CO3 · 10H2O.

subject: Science (Physics, Chemistry, Biology)
front_prompt: Why does dry HCl gas not change the color of dry litmus paper?
back_answer: Dry HCl gas does not dissociate into hydrogen ions (H+) in the absence of water, which is required to show acidic properties.

subject: Science (Physics, Chemistry, Biology)
front_prompt: What is the pH of a neutral solution at 298 K?

subject: Science (Physics, Chemistry, Biology)
front_prompt: Name the acid present in ant sting and give its chemical name.
back_answer: Methanoic acid (Formic acid), HCOOH.

subject: Science (Physics, Chemistry, Biology)
front_prompt: What happens when electricity is passed through an aqueous solution of sodium chloride (Brine)? Name the process.
back_answer: It decomposes to form sodium hydroxide, chlorine gas, and hydrogen gas. This process is called the Chlor-alkali process.

subject: Science (Physics, Chemistry, Biology)
front_prompt: What is the common name of CaOCl2?
back_answer: Bleaching powder

subject: Science (Physics, Chemistry, Biology)
front_prompt: Why should water never be added to concentrated acid?
back_answer: Adding water to concentrated acid is highly exothermic; the heat generated may cause the mixture to splash out and cause burns, or break the glass container.

subject: Science (Physics, Chemistry, Biology)
front_prompt: What is Plaster of Paris chemically? How is it prepared?
back_answer: Chemically, it is calcium sulphate hemihydrate (CaSO4 · 1/2H2O). It is prepared by heating gypsum (CaSO4 · 2H2O) at 373 K.

subject: Science (Physics, Chemistry, Biology)
front_prompt: State the general chemical reaction that occurs when an acid reacts with a metal.
back_answer: Acid + Metal -> Salt + Hydrogen gas

subject: Science (Physics, Chemistry, Biology)
front_prompt: What are olfactory indicators? Give one example.
back_answer: Indicators whose odor changes in acidic or basic media. Example: Vanilla extract, onion, or clove oil.

subject: Science (Physics, Chemistry, Biology)
front_prompt: What is the phenomenon of drawing metals into thin wires called?
back_answer: Ductility

subject: Science (Physics, Chemistry, Biology)
front_prompt: Name the non-metal that is lustrous (shiny).
back_answer: Iodine

subject: Science (Physics, Chemistry, Biology)
front_prompt: Which metal is liquid at room temperature?
back_answer: Mercury

subject: Science (Physics, Chemistry, Biology)
front_prompt: What is formed when a metal reacts with oxygen?
back_answer: Metal oxide (which is generally basic in nature)

subject: Science (Physics, Chemistry, Biology)
front_prompt: Give examples of amphoteric oxides.
back_answer: Aluminium oxide (Al2O3) and Zinc oxide (ZnO)

subject: Science (Physics, Chemistry, Biology)
front_prompt: Why do most metals not evolve hydrogen gas when reacted with nitric acid (HNO3)?
back_answer: Because nitric acid is a strong oxidizing agent that oxidizes the hydrogen produced to water and itself gets reduced to nitrogen oxides.

subject: Science (Physics, Chemistry, Biology)
front_prompt: What is the reactivity series of metals?
back_answer: A list of metals arranged in order of their decreasing activities.

subject: Science (Physics, Chemistry, Biology)
front_prompt: What is ionic bond (or electrovalent bond)?
back_answer: A bond formed by the transfer of electrons from a metal to a non-metal, resulting in electrostatic attraction between oppositely charged ions.

subject: Science (Physics, Chemistry, Biology)
front_prompt: What is the process of heating a carbonate ore strongly in the limited supply of air to convert it into metal oxide called?
back_answer: Calcination

subject: Science (Physics, Chemistry, Biology)
front_prompt: What is galvanisation?
back_answer: A method of protecting steel and iron from rusting by coating them with a thin layer of zinc.

subject: Science (Physics, Chemistry, Biology)
front_prompt: What are life processes?
back_answer: The basic functions performed by living organisms to maintain their life on earth and prevent damage and breakdowns.

subject: Science (Physics, Chemistry, Biology)
front_prompt: Define autotrophic nutrition.
back_answer: A mode of nutrition in which organisms prepare their own food from simple inorganic substances like carbon dioxide and water in the presence of sunlight and chlorophyll.

subject: Science (Physics, Chemistry, Biology)
front_prompt: What is the role of stomata in plants?
back_answer: Stomata are tiny pores on leaves used for gaseous exchange (oxygen and carbon dioxide) and transpiration.

subject: Science (Physics, Chemistry, Biology)
front_prompt: Name the enzyme present in human saliva and state its function.
back_answer: Salivary amylase; it breaks down complex starch into simple sugar (maltose).

subject: Science (Physics, Chemistry, Biology)
front_prompt: What is peristaltic movement?
back_answer: The rhythmic contraction and relaxation of the muscles of the alimentary canal that pushes food forward.

subject: Science (Physics, Chemistry, Biology)
front_prompt: What is the site of complete digestion of carbohydrates, proteins, and fats in humans?
back_answer: Small intestine.

subject: Science (Physics, Chemistry, Biology)
front_prompt: Define aerobic respiration.
back_answer: The breakdown of glucose in the presence of oxygen to release energy, producing carbon dioxide, water, and ATP.

subject: Science (Physics, Chemistry, Biology)
front_prompt: Why do muscle cramps occur during heavy exercise?
back_answer: Due to the accumulation of lactic acid produced by the anaerobic breakdown of pyruvate in muscle cells during oxygen deficiency.

subject: Science (Physics, Chemistry, Biology)
front_prompt: What is the function of the renal artery?
back_answer: To bring oxygenated and nitrogenous waste-containing blood from the aorta to the kidneys for filtration.

subject: Science (Physics, Chemistry, Biology)
front_prompt: What is the basic filtering unit of the human kidney?
back_answer: Nephron.

subject: Science (Physics, Chemistry, Biology)
front_prompt: What is the structural and functional unit of the nervous system?
back_answer: Neuron (or nerve cell)

subject: Science (Physics, Chemistry, Biology)
front_prompt: Which part of a neuron acquires information?
back_answer: Dendritic tip

subject: Science (Physics, Chemistry, Biology)
front_prompt: What is a synapse?
back_answer: The functional junction between the axon terminal of one neuron and the dendrite of the next neuron.

subject: Science (Physics, Chemistry, Biology)
front_prompt: Name the two main components of the central nervous system (CNS).
back_answer: Brain and Spinal Cord

subject: Science (Physics, Chemistry, Biology)
front_prompt: What is a reflex action?
back_answer: A sudden, involuntary response to a stimulus that protects the body from harm, controlled primarily by the spinal cord.

subject: Science (Physics, Chemistry, Biology)
front_prompt: Which part of the brain is responsible for precision of voluntary actions and maintaining posture and balance?
back_answer: Cerebellum

subject: Science (Physics, Chemistry, Biology)
front_prompt: Name the plant hormone that promotes cell division, especially in areas rapidly dividing like fruits and seeds.
back_answer: Cytokinin

subject: Science (Physics, Chemistry, Biology)
front_prompt: Which plant hormone inhibits growth and causes wilting of leaves?
back_answer: Abscisic acid (ABA)

subject: Science (Physics, Chemistry, Biology)
front_prompt: Which endocrine gland is known as the 'master gland' because it regulates other endocrine glands?
back_answer: Pituitary gland

subject: Science (Physics, Chemistry, Biology)
front_prompt: What is the function of insulin in the human body?
back_answer: It regulates (lowers) blood sugar levels.

subject: Science (Physics, Chemistry, Biology)
front_prompt: What is the primary difference between asexual and sexual reproduction?
back_answer: Asexual reproduction involves a single parent and produces genetically identical offspring (clones), whereas sexual reproduction involves two parents and introduces genetic variation through the fusion of gametes.

subject: Science (Physics, Chemistry, Biology)
front_prompt: Name the type of asexual reproduction commonly observed in Amoeba.
back_answer: Binary fission, where the parent cell divides into two equal-sized daughter cells.

subject: Science (Physics, Chemistry, Biology)
front_prompt: How does reproduction help in maintaining the stability of populations of species?
back_answer: Reproduction replaces the individuals lost due to death, maintaining a constant birth-to-death ratio and ensuring the survival and continuity of the species over time.

subject: Science (Physics, Chemistry, Biology)
front_prompt: What is vegetative propagation? Give one advantage.
back_answer: A method of asexual reproduction where new plants grow from vegetative parts of the plant like roots, stems, or leaves. Advantage: Plants grow faster, bear flowers and fruits earlier, and are genetically identical to the parent.

subject: Science (Physics, Chemistry, Biology)
front_prompt: Define pollination and state its two main types.
back_answer: Pollination is the transfer of pollen grains from the anther to the stigma of a flower. The two main types are self-pollination and cross-pollination.

subject: Science (Physics, Chemistry, Biology)
front_prompt: What is the function of the placenta in human females?
back_answer: The placenta is a disc-shaped tissue embedded in the uterine wall that provides glucose and oxygen from the mother's blood to the developing embryo, and removes waste substances from the embryo.

subject: Science (Physics, Chemistry, Biology)
front_prompt: List the male reproductive organs in humans.
back_answer: Testes, vas deferens, seminal vesicles, prostate gland, urethra, and penis.

subject: Science (Physics, Chemistry, Biology)
front_prompt: Name the hormone secreted by testes and ovaries respectively, and state one function of each.
back_answer: Testes secrete testosterone (regulates sperm production and secondary sexual characters in males); ovaries secrete estrogen (regulates egg maturation and secondary sexual characters in females).

subject: Science (Physics, Chemistry, Biology)
front_prompt: What are barrier methods of contraception? Give two examples.
back_answer: Methods that prevent physical meeting of sperm and ovum using physical barriers. Examples: Condoms and diaphragms (or cervical caps).

subject: Science (Physics, Chemistry, Biology)
front_prompt: Differentiate between regeneration and budding with examples.
back_answer: Regeneration is the ability of a fully grown organism to develop new individuals from its broken body parts (e.g., Planaria). Budding is the formation of a new organism from an outgrowth or bud on the parent body (e.g., Hydra or Yeast).

subject: Science (Physics, Chemistry, Biology)
front_prompt: Define heredity.
back_answer: The transmission of traits or characteristics from parents to their offspring generation after generation.

subject: Science (Physics, Chemistry, Biology)
front_prompt: What are variations?
back_answer: The differences in characters/traits shown by the individuals of a species and also between offspring of the same parents.

subject: Science (Physics, Chemistry, Biology)
front_prompt: Who is known as the 'Father of Genetics'?
back_answer: Gregor Johann Mendel

subject: Science (Physics, Chemistry, Biology)
front_prompt: Name the scientific name of the garden pea plant studied by Mendel.
back_answer: Pisum sativum

subject: Science (Physics, Chemistry, Biology)
front_prompt: What is a gene?
back_answer: A unit of DNA on a chromosome responsible for the inheritance of a specific trait.

subject: Science (Physics, Chemistry, Biology)
front_prompt: Distinguish between genotype and phenotype.
back_answer: Genotype is the genetic constitution of an organism, while phenotype is the observable physical or biochemical characteristic.

subject: Science (Physics, Chemistry, Biology)
front_prompt: State Mendel's Law of Segregation.
back_answer: Alleles separate during gamete formation so that each gamete carries only one allele for each gene.

subject: Science (Physics, Chemistry, Biology)
front_prompt: What is the phenotypic ratio in the F2 generation of a monohybrid cross?
back_answer: 3:1 (Three dominant to one recessive)

subject: Science (Physics, Chemistry, Biology)
front_prompt: What is the genotypic ratio in the F2 generation of a monohybrid cross?
back_answer: 1:2:1 (One homozygous dominant : Two heterozygous : One homozygous recessive)

subject: Science (Physics, Chemistry, Biology)
front_prompt: How is sex determined in human beings?
back_answer: Sex is determined by the type of sex chromosomes inherited from the father (an X chromosome leads to a female, a Y chromosome leads to a male).

subject: Science (Physics, Chemistry, Biology)
chapter: The Human Eye and the Colourful World
front_prompt: What is the part of the human eye that controls the amount of light entering it?
back_answer: Iris

subject: Science (Physics, Chemistry, Biology)
chapter: The Human Eye and the Colourful World
front_prompt: Define power of accommodation of the eye.
back_answer: The ability of the eye lens to adjust its focal length to focus objects at varying distances clearly on the retina.

subject: Science (Physics, Chemistry, Biology)
chapter: The Human Eye and the Colourful World
front_prompt: Name the defect of vision also known as nearsightedness and the lens used to correct it.
back_answer: Myopia; corrected using a concave lens.

subject: Science (Physics, Chemistry, Biology)
chapter: The Human Eye and the Colourful World
front_prompt: Why do stars twinkle at night?
back_answer: Due to atmospheric refraction of starlight by layers of varying refractive indices in the Earth's atmosphere.

subject: Science (Physics, Chemistry, Biology)
chapter: The Human Eye and the Colourful World
front_prompt: What is the phenomenon responsible for the blue color of the clear sky?
back_answer: Rayleigh scattering of light by air molecules and fine particles in the atmosphere.

subject: Science (Physics, Chemistry, Biology)
chapter: The Human Eye and the Colourful World
front_prompt: What is the near point of a normal human eye for a young adult?
back_answer: About 25 cm.

subject: Science (Physics, Chemistry, Biology)
chapter: The Human Eye and the Colourful World
front_prompt: Name the defect of vision in which a person can see distant objects clearly but cannot see nearby objects distinctly, and state its correction.
back_answer: Hypermetropia (farsightedness); corrected using a convex lens.

subject: Science (Physics, Chemistry, Biology)
chapter: The Human Eye and the Colourful World
front_prompt: What is dispersion of white light?
back_answer: The splitting of white light into its component seven colors when passing through a glass prism.

subject: Science (Physics, Chemistry, Biology)
chapter: The Human Eye and the Colourful World
front_prompt: Why are traffic signal lights red in color?
back_answer: Because red light has the maximum wavelength and is scattered the least by fog or smoke, making it visible from a long distance.

subject: Science (Physics, Chemistry, Biology)
chapter: The Human Eye and the Colourful World
front_prompt: What is presbyopia and how is it usually corrected?
back_answer: An age-related defect where accommodation power decreases; corrected using bifocal lenses.

subject: Science (Physics, Chemistry, Biology)
front_prompt: Who discovered that an electric current produces a magnetic field around it?
back_answer: Hans Christian Oersted in 1820.

subject: Science (Physics, Chemistry, Biology)
front_prompt: What is the pattern of magnetic field lines around a straight current-carrying conductor?
back_answer: Concentric circles centered on the wire, lying in planes perpendicular to the wire.

subject: Science (Physics, Chemistry, Biology)
front_prompt: State Maxwell's Right-Hand Thumb Rule.
back_answer: If you hold a current-carrying straight wire in your right hand such that your thumb points in the direction of current, then your fingers wrap around the wire in the direction of the magnetic field lines.

subject: Science (Physics, Chemistry, Biology)
front_prompt: What is a solenoid?
back_answer: A coil of many circular turns of insulated copper wire wrapped closely in the shape of a cylinder.

subject: Science (Physics, Chemistry, Biology)
front_prompt: What is an electromagnet?
back_answer: A strong magnetic field produced inside a solenoid used to magnetize a piece of magnetic material, like soft iron, placed inside the coil.

subject: Science (Physics, Chemistry, Biology)
front_prompt: State Fleming's Left-Hand Rule.
back_answer: Stretch the thumb, forefinger, and middle finger of your left hand such that they are mutually perpendicular. If the forefinger points in the direction of magnetic field and the middle finger in the direction of current, then the thumb points in the direction of force/motion.

subject: Science (Physics, Chemistry, Biology)
front_prompt: What is the principle of an electric motor?
back_answer: A current-carrying conductor placed in a magnetic field experiences a force, causing it to rotate (converts electrical energy into mechanical energy).

subject: Science (Physics, Chemistry, Biology)
front_prompt: What is electromagnetic induction?
back_answer: The phenomenon of producing an induced current in a coil due to a relative motion between a magnet and the coil (change in magnetic field).

subject: Science (Physics, Chemistry, Biology)
front_prompt: State Fleming's Right-Hand Rule.
back_answer: Stretch the thumb, forefinger, and middle finger of your right hand mutually perpendicular. If the forefinger points along the direction of magnetic field and the thumb points along the direction of motion of conductor, then the middle finger points in the direction of induced current.

subject: Science (Physics, Chemistry, Biology)
front_prompt: What are the three types of wires found in domestic electric circuits?
back_answer: Live wire (red insulation), Neutral wire (black insulation), and Earth wire (green insulation).

subject: Science (Physics, Chemistry, Biology)
front_prompt: Define ecosystem.
back_answer: An ecosystem consists of all the interacting organisms in an area together with the non-living components of the environment.

subject: Science (Physics, Chemistry, Biology)
front_prompt: What are the two main components of an ecosystem?
back_answer: Biotic (living) components and Abiotic (non-living) components.

subject: Science (Physics, Chemistry, Biology)
front_prompt: Distinguish between biodegradable and non-biodegradable substances with an example each.
back_answer: Biodegradable substances are broken down by biological processes (e.g., vegetable peels), whereas non-biodegradable substances are not broken down by biological agents (e.g., plastics).

subject: Science (Physics, Chemistry, Biology)
front_prompt: Define trophic levels.
back_answer: The specific trophic levels or steps in a food chain where energy transfer takes place are called trophic levels.

subject: Science (Physics, Chemistry, Biology)
front_prompt: State the 10% law of energy flow in an ecosystem.
back_answer: Only 10% of the energy is transferred from one trophic level to the next, while the remaining 90% is lost to the environment as heat.

subject: Science (Physics, Chemistry, Biology)
front_prompt: Why is the flow of energy in an ecosystem unidirectional?
back_answer: Energy captured by autotrophs does not revert back to the sun, and energy passed to herbivores does not go back to autotrophs; hence, energy flow is unidirectional.

subject: Science (Physics, Chemistry, Biology)
front_prompt: Define biological magnification (biomagnification).
back_answer: The progressive accumulation of harmful non-biodegradable chemicals (like pesticides) at successive trophic levels in a food chain is called biological magnification.

subject: Science (Physics, Chemistry, Biology)
front_prompt: What is ozone and how is it formed in the upper atmosphere?
back_answer: Ozone (O3) is a molecule formed by three atoms of oxygen. It is formed when UV radiations split molecular oxygen (O2) into free oxygen atoms, which then react with O2 molecules.

subject: Science (Physics, Chemistry, Biology)
front_prompt: What is the primary cause of ozone layer depletion?
back_answer: The primary cause is the release of chlorofluorocarbons (CFCs), used in refrigerants and fire extinguishers.

subject: Science (Physics, Chemistry, Biology)
front_prompt: Give one reason why food chains generally cannot have more than four or five trophic levels.
back_answer: Due to the massive loss of energy at each trophic level (10% law), very little usable energy remains after four or five trophic levels to sustain any higher level.

subject: Mathematics (Ganita Manjari) - Class 9 only

front_prompt: What are the two intersecting number lines used in a Cartesian coordinate system called?
back_answer: The X-axis (horizontal line) and the Y-axis (vertical line).

subject: Mathematics (Ganita Manjari) - Class 9 only
chapter: Orienting Yourself: The Use of Coordinates
front_prompt: What is the point of intersection of the X-axis and the Y-axis called?
back_answer: The origin, denoted by coordinates (0, 0).

subject: Mathematics (Ganita Manjari) - Class 9 only
chapter: Orienting Yourself: The Use of Coordinates
front_prompt: Into how many parts does the coordinate axes divide the plane, and what are these parts called?
back_answer: Four parts, called quadrants (Quadrants I, II, III, and IV).

subject: Mathematics (Ganita Manjari) - Class 9 only
chapter: Orienting Yourself: The Use of Coordinates
front_prompt: What is the x-coordinate of a point also known as?
back_answer: Abscissa.

subject: Mathematics (Ganita Manjari) - Class 9 only
chapter: Orienting Yourself: The Use of Coordinates
front_prompt: What is the y-coordinate of a point also known as?
back_answer: Ordinate.

subject: Mathematics (Ganita Manjari) - Class 9 only
chapter: Orienting Yourself: The Use of Coordinates
front_prompt: What are the signs of the coordinates (x, y) in the Second Quadrant (Quadrant II)?
back_answer: Negative x-coordinate and positive y-coordinate (-x, +y).

subject: Mathematics (Ganita Manjari) - Class 9 only
chapter: Orienting Yourself: The Use of Coordinates
front_prompt: What are the coordinates of any point lying on the X-axis?
back_answer: (x, 0), where x is the distance along the X-axis.

subject: Mathematics (Ganita Manjari) - Class 9 only
chapter: Orienting Yourself: The Use of Coordinates
front_prompt: What are the coordinates of any point lying on the Y-axis?
back_answer: (0, y), where y is the distance along the Y-axis.

subject: Mathematics (Ganita Manjari) - Class 9 only
chapter: Orienting Yourself: The Use of Coordinates
front_prompt: If a point has coordinates (-3, -5), in which quadrant does it lie?
back_answer: Third Quadrant (Quadrant III).

subject: Mathematics (Ganita Manjari) - Class 9 only
chapter: Orienting Yourself: The Use of Coordinates
front_prompt: Who is credited with developing the system of coordinates known as Cartesian geometry?
back_answer: René Descartes.

subject: Mathematics (Ganita Manjari) - Class 9 only
front_prompt: What is the general form of a linear polynomial in one variable?
back_answer: $ax + b$, where $a$ and $b$ are real numbers and $a \neq 0$.

subject: Mathematics (Ganita Manjari) - Class 9 only
front_prompt: What is the degree of a linear polynomial?

subject: Mathematics (Ganita Manjari) - Class 9 only
front_prompt: What is a zero (or root) of a polynomial $p(x)$?
back_answer: A real number $c$ such that $p(c) = 0$.

subject: Mathematics (Ganita Manjari) - Class 9 only
front_prompt: How many zeroes does a non-zero constant polynomial have?
back_answer: Zero (none)

subject: Mathematics (Ganita Manjari) - Class 9 only

subject: Mathematics (Ganita Manjari) - Class 9 only

subject: Mathematics (Ganita Manjari) - Class 9 only
front_prompt: In the linear polynomial $ax + b$, what condition must be met by coefficient $a$?
back_answer: $a \neq 0$ (if $a = 0$, it becomes a constant polynomial)

subject: Mathematics (Ganita Manjari) - Class 9 only
front_prompt: How many zeroes can a linear polynomial have at most?
back_answer: At most 1 zero (exactly one real zero)

subject: Mathematics (Ganita Manjari) - Class 9 only
front_prompt: Is $0$ a zero of the polynomial $p(x) = 5x$?
back_answer: Yes, because $p(0) = 5(0) = 0$.

subject: Mathematics (Ganita Manjari) - Class 9 only
front_prompt: What is the zero of the polynomial $p(x) = x - c$, where $c$ is a real number?
back_answer: $x = c$

subject: Mathematics (Ganita Manjari) - Class 9 only
front_prompt: What is a rational number?
back_answer: A number that can be expressed in the form p/q, where p and q are integers and q is not equal to 0.

subject: Mathematics (Ganita Manjari) - Class 9 only
front_prompt: Are all natural numbers also whole numbers?
back_answer: Yes, because the collection of whole numbers includes all natural numbers along with zero.

subject: Mathematics (Ganita Manjari) - Class 9 only
front_prompt: What is the decimal expansion of a rational number?
back_answer: It is either terminating or non-terminating repeating (recurring).

subject: Mathematics (Ganita Manjari) - Class 9 only
front_prompt: Define an irrational number.
back_answer: A number that cannot be expressed in the form p/q, where p and q are integers and q != 0; its decimal expansion is non-terminating and non-recurring.

subject: Mathematics (Ganita Manjari) - Class 9 only
front_prompt: What constitutes the collection of real numbers?
back_answer: The collection of all rational numbers and irrational numbers together.

subject: Mathematics (Ganita Manjari) - Class 9 only
front_prompt: Is every integer a rational number?
back_answer: Yes, every integer 'a' can be written as a/1, which is in the form p/q where q = 1 != 0.

subject: Mathematics (Ganita Manjari) - Class 9 only
front_prompt: How many rational numbers can be found between any two distinct rational numbers?
back_answer: Infinitely many rational numbers.

subject: Mathematics (Ganita Manjari) - Class 9 only
front_prompt: What is the nature of the decimal representation of sqrt(2)?
back_answer: Non-terminating and non-recurring, because sqrt(2) is an irrational number.

subject: Mathematics (Ganita Manjari) - Class 9 only
front_prompt: State whether the product of two irrational numbers is always irrational.
back_answer: False. The product of two irrational numbers can sometimes be a rational number (e.g., sqrt(2) * sqrt(2) = 2).

subject: Mathematics (Ganita Manjari) - Class 9 only
front_prompt: What does each point on the real number line represent?
back_answer: A unique real number.
