back_answer: It was a moral code of conduct based on universal ethics, non-violence, religious tolerance, respect for elders, and righteous living, rather than a specific religious dogma.

subject: History and Civics (H.C.G. Paper 1)
front_prompt: What were the officials appointed by Ashoka to propagate and monitor his Dhamma across the empire called?
back_answer: Dhamma-Mahamatras.

subject: History and Civics (H.C.G. Paper 1)
front_prompt: Name the National Emblem of India that is adopted from a Mauryan pillar.
back_answer: The Lion Capital of Ashoka at Sarnath.

subject: History and Civics (H.C.G. Paper 1)

back_answer: An assembly or academy of Tamil poets and scholars patronized by the Pandya kings of Madurai.

subject: History and Civics (H.C.G. Paper 1)

back_answer: The Cholas, the Cheras, and the Pandyas.

subject: History and Civics (H.C.G. Paper 1)

subject: History and Civics (H.C.G. Paper 1)

back_answer: Bow and Arrow

subject: History and Civics (H.C.G. Paper 1)

back_answer: Fish

subject: History and Civics (H.C.G. Paper 1)

back_answer: Karikala Chola

subject: History and Civics (H.C.G. Paper 1)
front_prompt: Who was the most celebrated Chera king known as 'Red Chera' or 'Good Chera'?
back_answer: Senguttuvan (The Good Chera)

subject: History and Civics (H.C.G. Paper 1)
front_prompt: What was the primary source of revenue for the Sangam kingdoms?
back_answer: Land revenue (known as Karai) and customs duties on foreign trade.

subject: History and Civics (H.C.G. Paper 1)
front_prompt: Name the famous ancient port city of the Cholas that served as a major center of international maritime trade.
back_answer: Puhar (also known as Kaveripattinam)

subject: History and Civics (H.C.G. Paper 1)
front_prompt: What major epic poem in Tamil literature describes the story of Kannagi and was written during or after the Sangam period?
back_answer: Silappadikaram (authored by Ilango Adigal)

subject: History and Civics (H.C.G. Paper 1)
front_prompt: Who was the founder of the Gupta Empire?
back_answer: Sri Gupta is generally considered the founder of the Gupta Empire, who assumed the title of Maharaja.

subject: History and Civics (H.C.G. Paper 1)
front_prompt: Who was the first Gupta ruler to assume the title of 'Maharajadhiraja'?
back_answer: Chandragupta I was the first Gupta ruler to assume the grand title of Maharajadhiraja (King of Kings).

subject: History and Civics (H.C.G. Paper 1)
front_prompt: Which Gupta ruler is known as the 'Napoleon of India' and why?
back_answer: Samudragupta is known as the 'Napoleon of India' due to his extensive military conquests and brilliant campaigns, as recorded by historian V.A. Smith.

subject: History and Civics (H.C.G. Paper 1)
front_prompt: Name the court poet of Samudragupta who composed the Allahabad Prasasti (Prayag Prashasti).
back_answer: Harishena was the court poet and minister of Samudragupta who composed the Allahabad Prasasti inscribed on an Ashokan pillar.

subject: History and Civics (H.C.G. Paper 1)
front_prompt: During whose reign did the famous Chinese pilgrim Faxian (Fa-Hien) visit India?
back_answer: Faxian visited India during the reign of Chandragupta II (Vikramaditya).

subject: History and Civics (H.C.G. Paper 1)
front_prompt: What title did Chandragupta II adopt after defeating the Shakas (Saka rulers of Western India)?
back_answer: Chandragupta II adopted the title of 'Vikramaditya' (Sun of Valour) and Sakari (Destroyer of Shakas).

subject: History and Civics (H.C.G. Paper 1)
front_prompt: Who was the brilliant astronomer and mathematician belonging to the Gupta period who stated that the Earth rotates on its axis?
back_answer: Aryabhata was the renowned mathematician and astronomer of the Gupta age who wrote 'Aryabhatiya'.

subject: History and Civics (H.C.G. Paper 1)
front_prompt: Name the famous Sanskrit playwright and poet known as one of the 'Navaratnas' (Nine Gems) in the court of Chandragupta II.
back_answer: Kalidasa, author of works like Abhijnanashakuntalam, Meghaduta, and Raghuvamsha.

subject: History and Civics (H.C.G. Paper 1)
front_prompt: What is the historical significance of the Mehrauli Iron Pillar near Qutb Minar in Delhi?
back_answer: It belongs to the Gupta period (associated with Chandragupta II) and is renowned for its remarkable rust-resistant technology, remaining completely unrusted for over 1,600 years.

subject: History and Civics (H.C.G. Paper 1)
front_prompt: Why is the Gupta period frequently described as the 'Golden Age' of ancient Indian history?
back_answer: Due to unprecedented progress in art, architecture, literature, science, mathematics, religious harmony, trade, and overall political stability.

subject: History and Civics (H.C.G. Paper 1)
front_prompt: Who was the founder of the Medieval Chola Empire (Imperial Cholas)?
back_answer: Vijayalaya

subject: History and Civics (H.C.G. Paper 1)
front_prompt: Which Chola ruler captured Madurai and assumed the title of 'Madurantaka'?
back_answer: Parantaka I

subject: History and Civics (H.C.G. Paper 1)
front_prompt: Name the famous Chola king who annexed Sri Lanka (Ceylon) and developed a powerful navy.
back_answer: Rajaraja I

subject: History and Civics (H.C.G. Paper 1)
front_prompt: Who built the famous Brihadeshwara Temple (Rajarajeshwara Temple) at Tanjore?
back_answer: Rajaraja I

subject: History and Civics (H.C.G. Paper 1)
front_prompt: Which Chola emperor extended the empire up to the Ganges and assumed the title 'Gangaikondachola'?
back_answer: Rajendra I

subject: History and Civics (H.C.G. Paper 1)
front_prompt: What was the capital city founded by Rajendra I after his northern expedition?
back_answer: Gangaikonda Cholapuram

subject: History and Civics (H.C.G. Paper 1)
front_prompt: What was the term used for the autonomous village assemblies in the Chola administration?
back_answer: Ur, Sabha, and Nagaram

subject: History and Civics (H.C.G. Paper 1)
front_prompt: Which inscription provides detailed information about the village administration and election system of the Cholas?
back_answer: The Uttiramerur Inscriptions

subject: History and Civics (H.C.G. Paper 1)
front_prompt: Into what administrative units was the Chola Empire divided, in descending order?
back_answer: Mandalam (Provinces) -> Valanadu -> Nadu -> Kurram (Village groups)

subject: History and Civics (H.C.G. Paper 1)
front_prompt: What was the standard currency/gold coin issued by the Cholas called?
back_answer: Kalanju

subject: History and Civics (H.C.G. Paper 1)
front_prompt: Which battle fought in 1191 AD marked the defeat of Muhammad Ghori by Prithviraj Chauhan?
back_answer: The First Battle of Tarain.

subject: History and Civics (H.C.G. Paper 1)
front_prompt: Name the decisive battle fought in 1192 AD that led to the establishment of Turkish rule in India.
back_answer: The Second Battle of Tarain.

subject: History and Civics (H.C.G. Paper 1)
front_prompt: Who was the founder of the Slave Dynasty (Mamluk Dynasty) in India in 1206 AD?
back_answer: Qutb-ud-din Aibak.

subject: History and Civics (H.C.G. Paper 1)
front_prompt: Which Sultan of Delhi is known for introducing the system of branding horses (Dagh) and maintaining a descriptive roll of soldiers (Chehra)?
back_answer: Ala-ud-din Khalji.

subject: History and Civics (H.C.G. Paper 1)
front_prompt: Who shifted the capital of the Delhi Sultanate from Delhi to Daulatabad (Devagiri) in 1327?
back_answer: Muhammad bin Tughluq.

subject: History and Civics (H.C.G. Paper 1)
front_prompt: Name the famous Moroccan traveller who visited India during the reign of Muhammad bin Tughluq and wrote 'Kitab-i-Rihla'.
back_answer: Ibn Battuta.

subject: History and Civics (H.C.G. Paper 1)
front_prompt: Who was the first and only female ruler of the Delhi Sultanate?
back_answer: Razia Sultana.

subject: History and Civics (H.C.G. Paper 1)
front_prompt: Which battle fought in 1526 AD marked the end of the Delhi Sultanate and the beginning of the Mughal Empire?
back_answer: The First Battle of Panipat.

subject: History and Civics (H.C.G. Paper 1)
front_prompt: Who wrote 'Tarikh-i-Firoz Shahi', an important historical chronicle of the Delhi Sultanate?
back_answer: Ziauddin Barani.

subject: History and Civics (H.C.G. Paper 1)
front_prompt: What was the term used during the Delhi Sultanate for revenue-free land grants given to religious scholars and pious persons?
back_answer: Madad-i-maash (or Waqf/Inam).

subject: History and Civics (H.C.G. Paper 1)
front_prompt: Who founded the Mughal Empire in India and in which year?
back_answer: Babur founded the Mughal Empire in 1526 after defeating Ibrahim Lodi in the First Battle of Panipat.

subject: History and Civics (H.C.G. Paper 1)
front_prompt: Name the two decisive battles fought by Babur that consolidated his rule in India.
back_answer: The First Battle of Panipat (1526) against Ibrahim Lodi and the Battle of Kanwah (1527) against Rana Sanga.

subject: History and Civics (H.C.G. Paper 1)
front_prompt: Who was Humayun's chief rival who temporarily drove the Mughals out of India?
back_answer: Sher Shah Suri, who established the Sur Empire after defeating Humayun at Chausa (1539) and Kannauj (1540).

subject: History and Civics (H.C.G. Paper 1)
front_prompt: At which battle and in what year did Akbar defeat Hemu to restore Mughal rule?
back_answer: The Second Battle of Panipat in 1556.

subject: History and Civics (H.C.G. Paper 1)
front_prompt: What was the name of the administrative and military system introduced by Akbar?
back_answer: The Mansabdari System.

subject: History and Civics (H.C.G. Paper 1)
front_prompt: Who was Akbar's finance minister who reformed the land revenue system through Zabt?
back_answer: Raja Todar Mal.

subject: History and Civics (H.C.G. Paper 1)
front_prompt: What was the name of the religious path or faith propounded by Akbar in 1582?
back_answer: Din-i Ilahi (Divine Faith), which promoted religious tolerance and synthesis.

subject: History and Civics (H.C.G. Paper 1)
front_prompt: Name the famous contemporary historian who wrote the 'Akbarnama' and 'Ain-i-Akbari'.
back_answer: Abul Fazl.

subject: History and Civics (H.C.G. Paper 1)
front_prompt: Which Mughal Emperor's reign is often referred to as the 'Golden Age' of Mughal architecture?
back_answer: Shah Jahan.

subject: History and Civics (H.C.G. Paper 1)
front_prompt: State two major factors that contributed to the decline of the Mughal Empire under Aurangzeb.
back_answer: Aurangzeb's religious orthodoxy (re-imposition of Jizya) and his prolonged, costly military campaigns in the Deccan.

subject: History and Civics (H.C.G. Paper 1)
front_prompt: What is meant by the 'Composite Culture' of Medieval India?
back_answer: It refers to the synthesis and blending of diverse cultural elements, traditions, art, architecture, languages, and religious beliefs of both Hindu and Muslim communities during the medieval period.

subject: History and Civics (H.C.G. Paper 1)
front_prompt: Who was the founder of the Bhakti movement in South India?
back_answer: Shankaracharya (Adi Shankara) initiated the revival of the Bhakti movement in South India through his philosophy of Advaita Vedanta.

subject: History and Civics (H.C.G. Paper 1)
front_prompt: Name the two major schools of saints in the Bhakti movement.
back_answer: The Saguna school (worship of a deity with attributes/form) and the Nirguna school (worship of a formless, abstract Supreme Being).

subject: History and Civics (H.C.G. Paper 1)
front_prompt: Who was Kabir and what was his core teaching?
back_answer: Kabir was a 15th-century mystic poet and saint who preached the unity of God, condemned ritualism, caste discrimination, and religious formalism, emphasizing love and devotion.

subject: History and Civics (H.C.G. Paper 1)
front_prompt: Who founded Sikhism, and what is the holy scripture of the Sikhs?
back_answer: Founded by Guru Nanak Dev Ji; the holy scripture is the Guru Granth Sahib.

subject: History and Civics (H.C.G. Paper 1)
front_prompt: What was the primary impact of the Sufi movement on medieval society?
back_answer: The Sufi movement promoted universal brotherhood, religious tolerance, love of God, and served as a bridge of understanding between Hindus and Muslims.

subject: History and Civics (H.C.G. Paper 1)
front_prompt: Name two prominent Sufi saints who settled in India.
back_answer: Khwaja Moinuddin Chishti (in Ajmer) and Nizamuddin Auliya (in Delhi).

subject: History and Civics (H.C.G. Paper 1)
front_prompt: Which new language evolved as a result of the interaction between Persians, Turks, Arabs, and local Indians during the medieval period?
back_answer: Urdu, often referred to as a 'camp language', evolved from the synthesis of Persian, Arabic, Turkish, and local Indian dialects like Khari Boli.

subject: History and Civics (H.C.G. Paper 1)
front_prompt: What architectural style emerged from the fusion of Indian and Islamic architectural features?
back_answer: The Indo-Islamic architectural style, characterized by the use of domes, arches, minarets, and intricate geometrical or floral carvings.

subject: History and Civics (H.C.G. Paper 1)
front_prompt: Give two examples of prominent monuments representing Indo-Islamic architecture.
back_answer: Qutb Minar and the Taj Mahal (or Agra Fort/Jama Masjid).

subject: History and Civics (H.C.G. Paper 1)
chapter: The Modern Age in Europe - Renaissance
front_prompt: What does the term 'Renaissance' literally mean?
back_answer: Rebirth

subject: History and Civics (H.C.G. Paper 1)
chapter: The Modern Age in Europe - Renaissance
front_prompt: Which city is considered the birthplace of the Renaissance?
back_answer: Florence, Italy

subject: History and Civics (H.C.G. Paper 1)
chapter: The Modern Age in Europe - Renaissance
front_prompt: Name the intellectual movement during the Renaissance that emphasized human value, agency, and potential rather than strictly religious dogma.
back_answer: Humanism

subject: History and Civics (H.C.G. Paper 1)
chapter: The Modern Age in Europe - Renaissance
front_prompt: Who invented the movable-type printing press around 1450, which helped spread Renaissance ideas rapidly across Europe?
back_answer: Johannes Gutenberg

subject: History and Civics (H.C.G. Paper 1)

back_answer: Leonardo da Vinci

subject: History and Civics (H.C.G. Paper 1)

back_answer: Michelangelo Buonarroti

subject: History and Civics (H.C.G. Paper 1)

front_prompt: Whose astronomical theory proposed that the Earth and other planets revolve around the Sun (Heliocentric theory), challenging the traditional geocentric view?
back_answer: Nicolaus Copernicus

subject: History and Civics (H.C.G. Paper 1)
chapter: The Modern Age in Europe - Renaissance
front_prompt: Which wealthy and influential banking family of Florence was the primary patron of arts and learning during the early Renaissance?
back_answer: The Medici family

subject: History and Civics (H.C.G. Paper 1)
chapter: The Modern Age in Europe - Renaissance
front_prompt: What major historical event in 1453 led to Greek scholars fleeing to Italy, bringing ancient classical texts and sparking the Renaissance?
back_answer: The Fall of Constantinople to the Ottoman Turks

subject: History and Civics (H.C.G. Paper 1)
chapter: The Modern Age in Europe - Renaissance
front_prompt: Who wrote the political treatise 'The Prince', which analyzed how political power is actually acquired and maintained?
back_answer: Niccolò Machiavelli

subject: History and Civics (H.C.G. Paper 1)
chapter: The Modern Age in Europe - Reformation
front_prompt: What was the Reformation?
back_answer: A 16th-century religious and political movement in Europe that aimed to reform the Roman Catholic Church and resulted in the establishment of Protestant churches.

subject: History and Civics (H.C.G. Paper 1)
chapter: The Modern Age in Europe - Reformation
front_prompt: Who initiated the Protestant Reformation in 1517?
back_answer: Martin Luther, a German monk and theology professor, who nailed his Ninety-Five Theses to the door of the Castle Church in Wittenberg.

subject: History and Civics (H.C.G. Paper 1)
chapter: The Modern Age in Europe - Reformation
front_prompt: What were 'Indulgences'?
back_answer: Certificates issued by the Roman Catholic Church that supposedly remitted the temporal punishment for sins in purgatory, often sold for money, which became a major cause of the Reformation.

subject: History and Civics (H.C.G. Paper 1)
chapter: The Modern Age in Europe - Reformation
front_prompt: Who was Johann Tetzel?
back_answer: A German Dominican friar notorious for selling indulgences in Germany to raise funds for the rebuilding of St. Peter's Basilica in Rome, sparking Martin Luther's protest.

subject: History and Civics (H.C.G. Paper 1)
chapter: The Modern Age in Europe - Reformation
front_prompt: What was the Diet of Worms (1521)?
back_answer: An assembly of the Holy Roman Empire convened by Emperor Charles V in Worms, Germany, where Martin Luther was ordered to recant his teachings and refused.

subject: History and Civics (H.C.G. Paper 1)
chapter: The Modern Age in Europe - Reformation
front_prompt: Who was John Calvin?
back_answer: A prominent French theologian and reformer who established a Protestant theocracy in Geneva, Switzerland, and advocated the doctrine of predestination.

subject: History and Civics (H.C.G. Paper 1)
chapter: The Modern Age in Europe - Reformation
front_prompt: What is the doctrine of 'Predestination'?
back_answer: The theological belief held by Calvinists that God has already determined from the beginning of time who will be saved (the elect) and who will be damned.

subject: History and Civics (H.C.G. Paper 1)
chapter: The Modern Age in Europe - Reformation
front_prompt: Which English monarch broke ties with the Roman Catholic Church to form the Church of England?
back_answer: King Henry VIII, primarily due to the Pope's refusal to annul his marriage to Catherine of Aragon.

subject: History and Civics (H.C.G. Paper 1)
chapter: The Modern Age in Europe - Reformation
front_prompt: What was the Counter-Reformation?
back_answer: A movement within the Roman Catholic Church in the 16th and 17th centuries to reform itself from within and halt the spread of Protestantism.

subject: History and Civics (H.C.G. Paper 1)
chapter: The Modern Age in Europe - Reformation
front_prompt: What was the significance of the invention of the printing press during the Reformation?
back_answer: It enabled the rapid and mass production of Martin Luther's German translation of the Bible and reform pamphlets, allowing ordinary people to read and interpret religious texts independently.

subject: History and Civics (H.C.G. Paper 1)
chapter: The Modern Age in Europe - Industrial Revolution
front_prompt: What was the Industrial Revolution?
back_answer: The transition from manual labor and hand tools to machine-driven manufacturing and factory systems, beginning in Great Britain in the 18th century.

subject: History and Civics (H.C.G. Paper 1)
chapter: The Modern Age in Europe - Industrial Revolution
front_prompt: Why did the Industrial Revolution begin in Great Britain first?
back_answer: Due to abundant coal and iron ore deposits, political stability, a strong colonial empire, a well-developed banking system, and favorable geographical positioning.

subject: History and Civics (H.C.G. Paper 1)
chapter: The Modern Age in Europe - Industrial Revolution
front_prompt: Who invented the Steam Engine and how did it impact the Industrial Revolution?
back_answer: James Watt improved the steam engine, which provided a reliable, continuous power source for factories and revolutionized transportation through railways and steamships.

subject: History and Civics (H.C.G. Paper 1)
chapter: The Modern Age in Europe - Industrial Revolution
front_prompt: What was the impact of the Industrial Revolution on the textile industry?
back_answer: Inventions like the Spinning Jenny (James Hargreaves) and the Power Loom (Edmund Cartwright) drastically sped up yarn production and weaving, shifting production from homes to large factories.

subject: History and Civics (H.C.G. Paper 1)
chapter: The Modern Age in Europe - Industrial Revolution
front_prompt: What were the major social consequences of the Industrial Revolution?
back_answer: The emergence of two distinct classes (capitalist bourgeoisie and wage-earning proletariat), rapid urbanization, poor working and living conditions, and the employment of women and children in hazardous factories.

subject: History and Civics (H.C.G. Paper 1)
chapter: The Modern Age in Europe - Industrial Revolution
front_prompt: How did the development of railways transform industry and trade?
back_answer: Railways enabled the swift and economical transport of heavy raw materials, manufactured goods, and passengers across vast distances, integrating national and international markets.

subject: History and Civics (H.C.G. Paper 1)
chapter: The Modern Age in Europe - Industrial Revolution
front_prompt: What role did the Enclosure Acts play in the Industrial Revolution?
back_answer: They privatized common lands in Britain, forcing small peasant farmers off their land and driving them to urban centers to become cheap wage labor for newly established factories.

subject: History and Civics (H.C.G. Paper 1)
chapter: The Modern Age in Europe - Industrial Revolution
front_prompt: What was the economic doctrine that gained prominence during the Industrial Revolution?
back_answer: Capitalism, characterized by private ownership of property, free markets, and minimal government intervention (laissez-faire).

subject: History and Civics (H.C.G. Paper 1)
chapter: The Modern Age in Europe - Industrial Revolution
front_prompt: What were 'Slums' in the context of the Industrial Revolution?
back_answer: Overcrowded, unsanitary urban residential areas near factories where the working class lived in extreme poverty with lack of clean water and proper sewage.

subject: History and Civics (H.C.G. Paper 1)
chapter: The Modern Age in Europe - Industrial Revolution
front_prompt: How did the Industrial Revolution lead to Imperialism?
back_answer: Industrialized European nations aggressively colonized Asia and Africa to secure cheap raw materials for their factories and captive markets to sell their mass-produced manufactured goods.

subject: History and Civics (H.C.G. Paper 1)
chapter: Our Constitution and Its Salient Features
front_prompt: What is meant by the term 'Constitution'?
back_answer: A Constitution is a foundational document or set of fundamental legal and political rules that defines the structure of a government, outlines the powers of its organs, and establishes the rights and duties of citizens.

subject: History and Civics (H.C.G. Paper 1)
chapter: Our Constitution and Its Salient Features
front_prompt: When was the Constitution of India adopted by the Constituent Assembly, and when did it come into force?
back_answer: It was adopted on November 26, 1949, and came into full force and effect on January 26, 1950 (Republic Day).

subject: History and Civics (H.C.G. Paper 1)
chapter: Our Constitution and Its Salient Features
front_prompt: Who was the Chairman of the Drafting Committee of the Constituent Assembly?
back_answer: Dr. B.R. Ambedkar

subject: History and Civics (H.C.G. Paper 1)
chapter: Our Constitution and Its Salient Features
front_prompt: Why is the Indian Constitution described as the 'longest written constitution' in the world?
back_answer: Due to India's vast diversity, historical legacy (Government of India Act 1935), detailed provisions for both the Union and the States, and specific safeguards for minorities and backward classes.

subject: History and Civics (H.C.G. Paper 1)
chapter: Our Constitution and Its Salient Features
front_prompt: What does the term 'Sovereign' signify in the Preamble to the Indian Constitution?
back_answer: It signifies that India is completely independent, internally supreme, and externally free from any foreign control or dominance.

subject: History and Civics (H.C.G. Paper 1)
chapter: Our Constitution and Its Salient Features
front_prompt: Define a 'Secular State' in the context of the Indian Constitution.
back_answer: A state that does not have any official or state religion, treats all religions equally, and guarantees freedom of conscience and worship to all individuals.

subject: History and Civics (H.C.G. Paper 1)
chapter: Our Constitution and Its Salient Features
front_prompt: What is meant by a 'Federal Polity' with a 'Unitary Bias'?
back_answer: India has a division of powers between the Centre and States (federal), but during emergencies or through specific constitutional provisions, the Central government becomes extremely powerful (unitary bias).

subject: History and Civics (H.C.G. Paper 1)
chapter: Our Constitution and Its Salient Features
front_prompt: What are Fundamental Rights, and in which part of the Constitution are they enshrined?
back_answer: Fundamental Rights are basic human rights guaranteed to all citizens by the Constitution for their holistic development. They are enshrined in Part III (Articles 12-35).

subject: History and Civics (H.C.G. Paper 1)
chapter: Our Constitution and Its Salient Features
front_prompt: What are Directive Principles of State Policy (DPSP), and where are they located?
back_answer: DPSP are guidelines or principles provided to the government for framing laws and establishing a social and economic democracy. They are located in Part IV (Articles 36-51) and borrowed from Ireland.

subject: History and Civics (H.C.G. Paper 1)
chapter: Our Constitution and Its Salient Features
front_prompt: What is meant by 'Universal Adult Franchise'?
back_answer: It means that every citizen of India who has attained the age of 18 years (lowered from 21 by the 61st Amendment) has the right to vote in elections without any discrimination based on caste, religion, gender, race, or wealth.

subject: History and Civics (H.C.G. Paper 1)
front_prompt: Which part of the Indian Constitution contains the Fundamental Rights?
back_answer: Part III (Articles 12 to 35) of the Indian Constitution.

subject: History and Civics (H.C.G. Paper 1)
front_prompt: From which country's constitution were the Fundamental Rights borrowed?
back_answer: The Constitution of the USA.

subject: History and Civics (H.C.G. Paper 1)
front_prompt: Why are Fundamental Rights called 'fundamental'?
back_answer: Because they are guaranteed and protected by the Constitution, which is the fundamental law of the land, and are essential for the all-round development of individuals.

subject: History and Civics (H.C.G. Paper 1)
front_prompt: Name the six Fundamental Rights enshrined in the Indian Constitution.
back_answer: 1. Right to Equality, 2. Right to Freedom, 3. Right against Exploitation, 4. Right to Freedom of Religion, 5. Cultural and Educational Rights, 6. Right to Constitutional Remedies.

subject: History and Civics (H.C.G. Paper 1)
front_prompt: Which Article guarantees the Right to Equality before Law and Equal Protection of Laws?
back_answer: Article 14 of the Indian Constitution.

subject: History and Civics (H.C.G. Paper 1)
front_prompt: Which Article abolishes untouchability and makes its practice in any form a punishable offense?
back_answer: Article 17.

subject: History and Civics (H.C.G. Paper 1)
front_prompt: Which Article guarantees freedom of speech and expression?
back_answer: Article 19(1)(a).

subject: History and Civics (H.C.G. Paper 1)
front_prompt: Which Article ensures free and compulsory education for children between the ages of 6 and 14 years?
back_answer: Article 21A.

subject: History and Civics (H.C.G. Paper 1)
front_prompt: Who described the 'Right to Constitutional Remedies' (Article 32) as the 'heart and soul of the Constitution'?
back_answer: Dr. B. R. Ambedkar.

subject: History and Civics (H.C.G. Paper 1)
front_prompt: Under which constitutional amendment and in which year were the Fundamental Duties added to the Constitution?
back_answer: The 42nd Constitutional Amendment Act, 1976.

subject: History and Civics (H.C.G. Paper 1)
front_prompt: In which part of the Indian Constitution are the Directive Principles of State Policy (DPSP) enshrined?
back_answer: Part IV (Articles 36 to 51) of the Indian Constitution.

subject: History and Civics (H.C.G. Paper 1)
front_prompt: From which country's constitution was the concept of Directive Principles of State Policy borrowed?
back_answer: The Constitution of Ireland (which had borrowed it from Spain).

subject: History and Civics (H.C.G. Paper 1)
front_prompt: Are the Directive Principles of State Policy justiciable in a court of law?
back_answer: No, they are non-justiciable, meaning they cannot be enforced by any court.

subject: History and Civics (H.C.G. Paper 1)
front_prompt: What is the primary objective of incorporating the Directive Principles in the Constitution?
back_answer: To establish a 'Welfare State' and achieve social and economic democracy in the country.

subject: History and Civics (H.C.G. Paper 1)
front_prompt: Which Article provides for the organization of Village Panchayats as units of self-government?
back_answer: Article 40.

subject: History and Civics (H.C.G. Paper 1)
front_prompt: What does Article 45 of the Directive Principles direct the State to provide?
back_answer: Early childhood care and education for all children until they complete the age of six years.

subject: History and Civics (H.C.G. Paper 1)
front_prompt: What does the principle of 'Equal pay for equal work for both men and women' under DPSP aim to ensure?
back_answer: Economic justice and removal of gender discrimination in remuneration.

subject: History and Civics (H.C.G. Paper 1)
front_prompt: Which Directive Principle promotes international peace and security (Article 51)?
back_answer: It directs the State to foster respect for international law, treaty obligations, and encourage settlement of international disputes by arbitration.

subject: History and Civics (H.C.G. Paper 1)
front_prompt: What is the key difference between Fundamental Rights and Directive Principles regarding legal enforcement?
back_answer: Fundamental Rights are justiciable (enforceable by courts), whereas Directive Principles are non-justiciable.

subject: History and Civics (H.C.G. Paper 1)
front_prompt: Which Article directs the State to separate the judiciary from the executive in the public services of the State?
back_answer: Article 50.

subject: History and Civics (H.C.G. Paper 1)
front_prompt: What is an election?
back_answer: An election is a formal and organized process through which citizens choose their representatives to govern the country.

subject: History and Civics (H.C.G. Paper 1)
front_prompt: Define direct election.
back_answer: An election in which voters directly choose their representatives to the legislature.

subject: History and Civics (H.C.G. Paper 1)
front_prompt: Define indirect election.
back_answer: An election in which voters elect representatives who in turn elect higher officials, such as the President of India.

subject: History and Civics (H.C.G. Paper 1)
front_prompt: What is Universal Adult Franchise?
back_answer: The right of all adult citizens (18 years and above) to vote in elections without discrimination based on caste, religion, gender, or wealth.

subject: History and Civics (H.C.G. Paper 1)
front_prompt: Name the constitutional body responsible for conducting free and fair elections in India.
back_answer: The Election Commission of India.

subject: History and Civics (H.C.G. Paper 1)
front_prompt: Under which Article of the Indian Constitution is the Election Commission established?
back_answer: Article 324.

subject: History and Civics (H.C.G. Paper 1)
front_prompt: Who appoints the Chief Election Commissioner and other Election Commissioners in India?
back_answer: The President of India.

subject: History and Civics (H.C.G. Paper 1)
front_prompt: What is the tenure of office for the Chief Election Commissioner?
back_answer: 6 years or until they attain the age of 65 years, whichever is earlier.

subject: History and Civics (H.C.G. Paper 1)
front_prompt: What does EVM stand for in the context of Indian elections?
back_answer: Electronic Voting Machine.

subject: History and Civics (H.C.G. Paper 1)
front_prompt: What is the primary objective of the Model Code of Conduct?
back_answer: To ensure that political parties and candidates adhere to ethical standards and prevent misuse of official machinery during elections.

subject: History and Civics (H.C.G. Paper 1)
front_prompt: What is meant by Local Self-Government?
back_answer: Local Self-Government is the management of local affairs by local bodies elected by the local people.

subject: History and Civics (H.C.G. Paper 1)
front_prompt: Which Constitutional Amendment Acts gave statutory status to the Panchayati Raj and Urban Local Bodies in India?
back_answer: The 73rd Constitutional Amendment Act (for Rural) and the 74th Constitutional Amendment Act (for Urban), 1992.

subject: History and Civics (H.C.G. Paper 1)
front_prompt: Name the three tiers of the Panchayati Raj system in India.
back_answer: 1. Gram Panchayat (Village level), 2. Panchayat Samiti (Block level), 3. Zilla Parishad (District level).

subject: History and Civics (H.C.G. Paper 1)
front_prompt: What is the primary body of local self-government at the village level?
back_answer: Gram Panchayat.

subject: History and Civics (H.C.G. Paper 1)
front_prompt: Who constitutes the Gram Sabha?
back_answer: All adult residents (voters) registered in the electoral rolls of a village within the jurisdiction of a Gram Panchayat.

subject: History and Civics (H.C.G. Paper 1)
front_prompt: Who is the elected head of a Gram Panchayat?
back_answer: Sarpanch or Panchayat President.

subject: History and Civics (H.C.G. Paper 1)
front_prompt: What is the apex body of the Panchayati Raj system at the district level?
back_answer: Zilla Parishad.

subject: History and Civics (H.C.G. Paper 1)
front_prompt: What is the urban local self-government body established for a large city?
back_answer: Municipal Corporation (Nagar Nigam).

subject: History and Civics (H.C.G. Paper 1)
front_prompt: What is the elected head of a Municipal Corporation called?
back_answer: Mayor.

subject: History and Civics (H.C.G. Paper 1)
front_prompt: Who is the chief executive officer of a Municipal Corporation appointed by the State Government?
back_answer: Municipal Commissioner.

subject: History and Civics (H.C.G. Paper 1)
front_prompt: What are the two Houses of the Indian Parliament?
back_answer: The Lok Sabha (House of the People) and the Rajya Sabha (Council of States).

subject: History and Civics (H.C.G. Paper 1)
front_prompt: What is the maximum strength of the Lok Sabha as per the Constitution?
back_answer: 552 members (530 from States, 20 from Union Territories, and up to 2 nominated Anglo-Indian members, though the Anglo-Indian nomination was discontinued by the 104th Constitutional Amendment Act).

subject: History and Civics (H.C.G. Paper 1)
front_prompt: What is the maximum strength of the Rajya Sabha?
back_answer: 250 members, out of which 238 represent States and Union Territories, and 12 are nominated by the President from persons having special knowledge or practical experience in literature, science, art, and social service.

subject: History and Civics (H.C.G. Paper 1)
front_prompt: What is the normal term of office for the Lok Sabha?
back_answer: 5 years, unless dissolved earlier by the President.

subject: History and Civics (H.C.G. Paper 1)
front_prompt: Why is the Rajya Sabha called a permanent House?
back_answer: Because it is not subject to dissolution; one-third of its members retire every two years, and new members are elected to fill their seats.

subject: History and Civics (H.C.G. Paper 1)
front_prompt: What are the qualifications required to be a member of the Lok Sabha?
back_answer:
1. Must be a citizen of India. 
2. Must not be less than 25 years of age. 
3. Must have his/her name in the electoral rolls in any part of the country. 
4. Must not hold any office of profit.

subject: History and Civics (H.C.G. Paper 1)
front_prompt: What are the qualifications required to be a member of the Rajya Sabha?
back_answer:
1. Must be a citizen of India. 
2. Must not be less than 30 years of age. 
3. Must be a registered voter in the State/UT they represent. 
4. Must not hold any office of profit.

subject: History and Civics (H.C.G. Paper 1)
front_prompt: Who is the ex-officio Chairman of the Rajya Sabha?
back_answer: The Vice-President of India.

subject: History and Civics (H.C.G. Paper 1)
front_prompt: What is meant by 'Quorum' in the context of Parliament?
back_answer: Quorum is the minimum number of members required to be present in the House to transact business, which is one-tenth (1/10th) of the total membership of each House.

subject: History and Civics (H.C.G. Paper 1)
front_prompt: What is a Money Bill and where can it be introduced?
back_answer: A Money Bill is a bill concerned exclusively with financial matters like taxation, borrowing, or expenditure from the Consolidated Fund of India. It can be introduced only in the Lok Sabha.

subject: History and Civics (H.C.G. Paper 1)
chapter: The Union Executive (The President, Vice-President, Prime Minister and Council of Ministers)
front_prompt: Who constitutes the Union Executive in India?
back_answer: The President, the Vice-President, the Prime Minister, and the Council of Ministers.

subject: History and Civics (H.C.G. Paper 1)
chapter: The Union Executive (The President, Vice-President, Prime Minister and Council of Ministers)
front_prompt: What is the maximum age limit for election to the office of the President of India?
back_answer: There is no maximum age limit, provided the candidate is at least 35 years of age.

subject: History and Civics (H.C.G. Paper 1)
chapter: The Union Executive (The President, Vice-President, Prime Minister and Council of Ministers)
front_prompt: Name the electoral college that elects the President of India.
back_answer: Elected members of both Houses of Parliament (Lok Sabha and Rajya Sabha) and elected members of the Legislative Assemblies (Vidhan Sabha) of all States and Union Territories of Delhi and Puducherry.

subject: History and Civics (H.C.G. Paper 1)
chapter: The Union Executive (The President, Vice-President, Prime Minister and Council of Ministers)
front_prompt: What is the procedure called by which the President of India can be removed from office?
back_answer: Impeachment.

subject: History and Civics (H.C.G. Paper 1)
chapter: The Union Executive (The President, Vice-President, Prime Minister and Council of Ministers)
front_prompt: Under what article can the President of India proclaim a National Emergency?
back_answer: Article 352.

subject: History and Civics (H.C.G. Paper 1)
chapter: The Union Executive (The President, Vice-President, Prime Minister and Council of Ministers)
front_prompt: Who acts as the ex-officio Chairman of the Rajya Sabha?
back_answer: The Vice-President of India.

subject: History and Civics (H.C.G. Paper 1)
chapter: The Union Executive (The President, Vice-President, Prime Minister and Council of Ministers)
front_prompt: Who appoints the Prime Minister of India?
back_answer: The President of India.

subject: History and Civics (H.C.G. Paper 1)
chapter: The Union Executive (The President, Vice-President, Prime Minister and Council of Ministers)
front_prompt: What is the collective responsibility of the Council of Ministers?
back_answer: The Council of Ministers is collectively responsible to the Lok Sabha; they swim together and sink together.

subject: History and Civics (H.C.G. Paper 1)
chapter: The Union Executive (The President, Vice-President, Prime Minister and Council of Ministers)
front_prompt: What is the term used for the discretionary power of the President to withhold assent to a Bill passed by Parliament?
back_answer: Veto Power (specifically, Pocket Veto or Absolute Veto).

subject: History and Civics (H.C.G. Paper 1)
chapter: The Union Executive (The President, Vice-President, Prime Minister and Council of Ministers)
front_prompt: Who serves as the principal link between the President and the Council of Ministers?
back_answer: The Prime Minister.

subject: History and Civics (H.C.G. Paper 1)
chapter: The Judiciary (The Supreme Court, High Courts and Subordinate Courts)
front_prompt: What is the highest court of appeal in India?
back_answer: The Supreme Court of India.

subject: History and Civics (H.C.G. Paper 1)
chapter: The Judiciary (The Supreme Court, High Courts and Subordinate Courts)
front_prompt: At what age does a judge of the Supreme Court of India retire?
back_answer: 65 years of age.

subject: History and Civics (H.C.G. Paper 1)
chapter: The Judiciary (The Supreme Court, High Courts and Subordinate Courts)
front_prompt: Who appoints the Chief Justice and other judges of the Supreme Court?
back_answer: The President of India.

subject: History and Civics (H.C.G. Paper 1)
chapter: The Judiciary (The Supreme Court, High Courts and Subordinate Courts)
front_prompt: What is the retirement age of a High Court judge?
back_answer: 62 years of age.

subject: History and Civics (H.C.G. Paper 1)
chapter: The Judiciary (The Supreme Court, High Courts and Subordinate Courts)
front_prompt: Define Original Jurisdiction of the Supreme Court.
back_answer: The power of the Supreme Court to hear and decide disputes in the first instance, such as disputes between the Centre and one or more States, or between two or more States.

subject: History and Civics (H.C.G. Paper 1)
chapter: The Judiciary (The Supreme Court, High Courts and Subordinate Courts)
front_prompt: What is meant by Appellate Jurisdiction of the High Court?
back_answer: The power of the High Court to hear appeals against judgments, decrees, or orders of subordinate courts in civil and criminal matters.

subject: History and Civics (H.C.G. Paper 1)
chapter: The Judiciary (The Supreme Court, High Courts and Subordinate Courts)
front_prompt: What are writs issued for the enforcement of Fundamental Rights called?
back_answer: Prerogative writs (such as Habeas Corpus, Mandamus, Prohibition, Certiorari, and Quo-Warranto).

subject: History and Civics (H.C.G. Paper 1)
chapter: The Judiciary (The Supreme Court, High Courts and Subordinate Courts)
front_prompt: What is the primary function of Judicial Review?
back_answer: The power of the judiciary to examine the constitutional validity of legislative enactments and executive orders, and declare them void if they violate the Constitution.

subject: History and Civics (H.C.G. Paper 1)
chapter: The Judiciary (The Supreme Court, High Courts and Subordinate Courts)
front_prompt: Who is the highest judicial authority in a district?
back_answer: The District Judge.

subject: History and Civics (H.C.G. Paper 1)
chapter: The Judiciary (The Supreme Court, High Courts and Subordinate Courts)
front_prompt: What does being a 'Court of Record' mean for the Supreme Court and High Courts?
back_answer: Their judgments and proceedings are recorded for perpetual memory and testimony, and they have the power to punish for contempt of court.

subject: History and Civics (H.C.G. Paper 1)
front_prompt: When did the First War of Independence break out?

subject: History and Civics (H.C.G. Paper 1)
front_prompt: Name the policy introduced by Lord Dalhousie under which the kingdom of Jhansi was annexed.
back_answer: Doctrine of Lapse

subject: History and Civics (H.C.G. Paper 1)
front_prompt: Who was proclaimed as the Emperor of India by the rebels in Delhi during the 1857 revolt?
back_answer: Bahadur Shah Zafar

subject: History and Civics (H.C.G. Paper 1)
front_prompt: Which sepoy at Barrackpore refused to use the greased cartridge and attacked British officers on March 29, 1857?
back_answer: Mangal Pandey

subject: History and Civics (H.C.G. Paper 1)
front_prompt: Name the Act passed in 1856 that made it compulsory for new recruits of the Bengal Army to serve overseas if required.
back_answer: General Service Enlistment Act

subject: History and Civics (H.C.G. Paper 1)
front_prompt: Which British Governor-General annexed Awadh in 1856 on the grounds of alleged misgovernance?
back_answer: Lord Dalhousie

subject: History and Civics (H.C.G. Paper 1)
front_prompt: Who led the uprising of 1857 from Kanpur and was also known as Dhondu Pant?
back_answer: Nana Saheb

subject: History and Civics (H.C.G. Paper 1)
front_prompt: Name the Act passed in 1858 that ended the rule of the East India Company and transferred power to the British Crown.
back_answer: Government of India Act 1858

subject: History and Civics (H.C.G. Paper 1)
front_prompt: Who was the brilliant military commander of Nana Saheb who continued guerrilla warfare after the fall of Kanpur?
back_answer: Tantia Tope

subject: History and Civics (H.C.G. Paper 1)
front_prompt: What title was created by the Act of 1858 to represent the British monarch in India instead of the Governor-General?
back_answer: Viceroy

subject: History and Civics (H.C.G. Paper 1)
front_prompt: What is meant by 'Nationalism'?
back_answer: A strong feeling of patriotism, unity, and love for one's motherland, accompanied by a shared consciousness of common history, culture, and political aspirations.

subject: History and Civics (H.C.G. Paper 1)
front_prompt: Name the Governor-General whose repressive policies and Acts acted as a catalyst for the growth of Indian nationalism.
back_answer: Lord Lytton

subject: History and Civics (H.C.G. Paper 1)
front_prompt: What was the objective and year of the Vernacular Press Act?
back_answer: Passed in 1878 to curb the freedom of the Indian-language press and prevent criticism of British policies.

subject: History and Civics (H.C.G. Paper 1)
front_prompt: What was the purpose of the Arms Act of 1878?
back_answer: It made it a criminal offence for Indians to keep, carry, or manufacture firearms without a license, while Europeans were exempted.

subject: History and Civics (H.C.G. Paper 1)
front_prompt: What controversy during Lord Ripon's tenure exposed racial prejudice among the British and united Indians against them?
back_answer: The Ilbert Bill Controversy (1883)

subject: History and Civics (H.C.G. Paper 1)
front_prompt: How did Western education contribute to the rise of Indian nationalism?
back_answer: It introduced Indians to modern ideas of liberty, equality, democracy, and nationalism, and provided a common English language medium for communication among educated Indians from different regions.

subject: History and Civics (H.C.G. Paper 1)
front_prompt: Name two prominent socio-religious reform movements of the 19th century that fostered national pride and unity.
back_answer: Brahmo Samaj (founded by Raja Ram Mohan Roy) and Arya Samaj (founded by Swami Dayanand Saraswati).

subject: History and Civics (H.C.G. Paper 1)
front_prompt: How did the development of railways and telegraphs help in the growth of nationalism in India?
back_answer: They facilitated rapid movement of people, ideas, and news across the country, breaking down regional barriers and bringing leaders together.

subject: History and Civics (H.C.G. Paper 1)
front_prompt: What role did the rediscovery of India's past play in fostering national awakening?
back_answer: Archaeological discoveries (like those by Max Mueller and the ASI) revealed India's glorious heritage in art, science, and philosophy, restoring national self-respect and confidence.

subject: History and Civics (H.C.G. Paper 1)
front_prompt: What was the economic impact of British rule that fueled anti-British feelings among Indians?
back_answer: Drain of wealth, destruction of traditional Indian handicrafts and cottage industries, heavy taxation, and recurring famines caused by exploitative economic policies.

subject: History and Civics (H.C.G. Paper 1)
chapter: First Phase of the Indian National Movement (1885-1907)
front_prompt: When and where was the first session of the Indian National Congress held, and who was its first President?
back_answer: Held in December 1885 at Gokuldas Tejpal Sanskrit College in Bombay; presided over by W.C. Bonnerjee.

subject: History and Civics (H.C.G. Paper 1)
chapter: First Phase of the Indian National Movement (1885-1907)
front_prompt: Who is regarded as the founder of the Indian National Congress, and in which year was it formed?
back_answer: Allan Octavian Hume (A.O. Hume) in 1885.

subject: History and Civics (H.C.G. Paper 1)
chapter: First Phase of the Indian National Movement (1885-1907)
front_prompt: Name any three prominent Early Nationalists (Moderates) of the Indian National Congress.
back_answer: Dadabhai Naoroji, Surendranath Banerjee, and Gopal Krishna Gokhale.

subject: History and Civics (H.C.G. Paper 1)
chapter: First Phase of the Indian National Movement (1885-1907)
front_prompt: What were the primary methods adopted by the Early Nationalists during their phase of the movement?
back_answer: Constitutional and peaceful methods such as prayers, petitions, meetings, speeches, and memorandums (the 3Ps: Prayer, Petition, and Protest).

subject: History and Civics (H.C.G. Paper 1)
chapter: First Phase of the Indian National Movement (1885-1907)
front_prompt: Who is known as the 'Grand Old Man of India', and which book did he author to propagate the Drain Theory?
back_answer: Dadabhai Naoroji; he authored the book 'Poverty and Un-British Rule in India'.

subject: History and Civics (H.C.G. Paper 1)
chapter: First Phase of the Indian National Movement (1885-1907)
front_prompt: What was the main economic grievance highlighted by the Early Nationalists against British rule?
back_answer: The economic drain of India's wealth to Britain through heavy taxation, unfair trade policies, and home charges.

subject: History and Civics (H.C.G. Paper 1)
chapter: First Phase of the Indian National Movement (1885-1907)
front_prompt: State two key achievements or contributions of the Early Nationalists.
back_answer: 1. Created national awakening and political consciousness among Indians. 2. Exposed the exploitative economic nature of British rule through the Drain Theory.

subject: History and Civics (H.C.G. Paper 1)
chapter: First Phase of the Indian National Movement (1885-1907)
front_prompt: Why were the Early Nationalists sometimes criticized as 'Moderate' or practicing 'Political Mendicancy'?
back_answer: Because of their moderate approach, reliance on petitions and appeals to the British sense of justice, and failure to secure immediate major political concessions.

subject: History and Civics (H.C.G. Paper 1)
chapter: First Phase of the Indian National Movement (1885-1907)
front_prompt: Who was regarded as the political guru of Mahatma Gandhi and founded the Servants of India Society in 1905?
back_answer: Gopal Krishna Gokhale.

subject: History and Civics (H.C.G. Paper 1)
chapter: First Phase of the Indian National Movement (1885-1907)
front_prompt: What was the official British attitude toward the Indian National Congress in its initial years?
back_answer: Initially benevolent and supportive (hoping it would act as a safety valve), but later hostile as the Congress grew critical of British administration.

subject: History and Civics (H.C.G. Paper 1)
chapter: Second Phase of the Indian National Movement (1905-1916)
front_prompt: Who announced the Partition of Bengal and in which year?
back_answer: Lord Curzon announced the Partition of Bengal in July 1905 (implemented on October 16, 1905).

subject: History and Civics (H.C.G. Paper 1)
chapter: Second Phase of the Indian National Movement (1905-1916)
front_prompt: State the twin objectives behind the Partition of Bengal as claimed by the British.
back_answer: To bring administrative efficiency to the large and unwieldy province of Bengal and to relieve the Bengal government of its heavy burden.

subject: History and Civics (H.C.G. Paper 1)
chapter: Second Phase of the Indian National Movement (1905-1916)
front_prompt: What was the actual political motive (the real motive) behind the Partition of Bengal?
back_answer: To crush the rising nationalist movement in Bengal and implement the policy of 'Divide and Rule' by dividing Hindus and Muslims.

subject: History and Civics (H.C.G. Paper 1)
chapter: Second Phase of the Indian National Movement (1905-1916)
front_prompt: Name the prominent extremist leaders known as the 'Lal-Bal-Pal' trio.
back_answer: Lala Lajpat Rai, Bal Gangadhar Tilak, and Bipin Chandra Pal.

subject: History and Civics (H.C.G. Paper 1)
chapter: Second Phase of the Indian National Movement (1905-1916)
front_prompt: When and where was the Muslim League founded?
back_answer: Founded on December 30, 1906, at Dacca (Dhaka).

subject: History and Civics (H.C.G. Paper 1)
chapter: Second Phase of the Indian National Movement (1905-1916)
front_prompt: State two primary objectives of the Muslim League at its inception.
back_answer: 1. To promote among Indian Muslims feelings of loyalty to the British Government. 2. To protect and advance the political rights and interests of Muslims in India.

subject: History and Civics (H.C.G. Paper 1)
chapter: Second Phase of the Indian National Movement (1905-1916)
front_prompt: Mention two methods advocated by the Assertive (Radical) Nationalists.
back_answer: Swadeshi (use of indigenous goods), Boycott (of foreign goods), National Education, and Passive Resistance.

subject: History and Civics (H.C.G. Paper 1)
chapter: Second Phase of the Indian National Movement (1905-1916)
front_prompt: What was the significance of the Lucknow Pact of 1916?
back_answer: It marked the reunion of the Moderates and Assertive wings of the Congress and established a joint political front between the Indian National Congress and the Muslim League.

subject: History and Civics (H.C.G. Paper 1)
chapter: Second Phase of the Indian National Movement (1905-1916)
front_prompt: Who declared 'Swaraj is my birthright and I shall have it'?
back_answer: Bal Gangadhar Tilak.

subject: History and Civics (H.C.G. Paper 1)
chapter: Second Phase of the Indian National Movement (1905-1916)
front_prompt: Name the two Home Rule Leagues established in India and their founders.
back_answer: 1. Indian Home Rule League founded by Bal Gangadhar Tilak (April 1916). 2. Home Rule League founded by Annie Besant (September 1916).

subject: History and Civics (H.C.G. Paper 1)
chapter: Mahatma Gandhi and the National Movement
front_prompt: When and where did Mahatma Gandhi return to India from South Africa, and which leader did he regard as his political guru?
back_answer: Gandhi returned to India in January 1915, and he regarded Gopal Krishna Gokhale as his political guru.

subject: History and Civics (H.C.G. Paper 1)
chapter: Mahatma Gandhi and the National Movement
front_prompt: Name the three early local movements led by Mahatma Gandhi in India between 1917 and 1918 along with their respective regions.
back_answer:
1. Champaran Satyagraha (Bihar, 1917)
2. Kheda Satyagraha (Gujarat, 1918)
3. Ahmedabad Mill Workers' Strike (Gujarat, 1918)

subject: History and Civics (H.C.G. Paper 1)
chapter: Mahatma Gandhi and the National Movement
front_prompt: What was the primary grievance of the peasants in the Champaran Satyagraha (1917)?
back_answer: European planters forced Indian peasants to cultivate indigo on 3/20th of their land under the oppressive Tinkathia system.

subject: History and Civics (H.C.G. Paper 1)
chapter: Mahatma Gandhi and the National Movement
front_prompt: What was the Rowlatt Act (1919) and why was it fiercely opposed by Indians?
back_answer: It was an act passed by the Imperial Legislative Council that allowed arrest without warrant and detention of political prisoners for up to two years without trial, dubbed 'No Dalil, No Vakil, No Appeal'.

subject: History and Civics (H.C.G. Paper 1)
chapter: Mahatma Gandhi and the National Movement
front_prompt: Give the date, location, and key perpetrator of the Jallianwala Bagh Massacre.
back_answer:

subject: Mathematics
front_prompt: What is a replacement set in the context of linear inequations?
back_answer: The set of numbers from which the values of the variable involved in the inequation are chosen.

subject: Mathematics
front_prompt: Define the solution set of an inequation.
back_answer: The subset of the replacement set whose elements satisfy the given inequation.

subject: Mathematics
front_prompt: What happens to the inequality sign when both sides of an inequation are multiplied or divided by a negative number?
back_answer: The inequality sign is reversed (e.g., '<' becomes '>', and '≤' becomes '≥').

subject: Mathematics
front_prompt: How does adding or subtracting the same number from both sides affect an inequality?
back_answer: The inequality remains unchanged; the direction of the inequality sign stays the same.

subject: Mathematics
front_prompt: What type of circle is used on a number line to represent strict inequalities like '<' or '>'?
back_answer: A hollow (unshaded) circle, indicating that the boundary point is not included in the solution set.

subject: Mathematics
front_prompt: What type of circle is used on a number line to represent slack inequalities like '≤' or '≥'?
back_answer: A solid (shaded) circle, indicating that the boundary point is included in the solution set.

subject: Mathematics
front_prompt: How are solutions representing 'real numbers' depicted on a number line?
back_answer: By a thick, continuous line segment or ray covering all intermediate points within the solution range.

subject: Mathematics
front_prompt: How are solutions representing 'integers' or 'natural numbers' depicted on a number line?
back_answer: By discrete points (dots) marked at the respective integer or natural number values.

subject: Mathematics
front_prompt: Solve for x: 3x - 4 < 2, given that the replacement set is the set of integers (Z).

subject: Mathematics
front_prompt: If -2x ≤ 6 and the replacement set is R (real numbers), what is the solution set?

subject: Mathematics
front_prompt: State the Remainder Theorem.
back_answer: If $f(x)$ is a polynomial of degree $\geq 1$ and is divided by a linear polynomial $(x - a)$, then the remainder is equal to $f(a)$.

subject: Mathematics
front_prompt: State the Factor Theorem.
back_answer: If $f(x)$ is a polynomial of degree $\geq 1$ and $a$ is a real number such that $f(a) = 0$, then $(x - a)$ is a factor of $f(x)$. Conversely, if $(x - a)$ is a factor of $f(x)$, then $f(a) = 0$.

subject: Mathematics
front_prompt: What is the remainder when a polynomial $f(x)$ is divided by $(ax + b)$?
back_answer: The remainder is given by $f\left(-\frac{b}{a}\right)$.

subject: Mathematics
front_prompt: If $(2x - 1)$ is a factor of the polynomial $f(x)$, what is the value of $f\left(\frac{1}{2}\right)$?
back_answer: $f\left(\frac{1}{2}\right) = 0$, according to the Factor Theorem.

subject: Mathematics

subject: Mathematics
front_prompt: What is the degree of the remainder obtained when a polynomial $f(x)$ is divided by a linear polynomial $(x - a)$?
back_answer: The degree of the remainder is $0$ (i.e., a constant value).

subject: Mathematics

subject: Physics (Science Paper 1)
front_prompt: Define Force.
back_answer: A force is an external push or pull that changes or tends to change the state of rest or uniform motion of a body, changes its direction of motion, or alters its shape and size.

subject: Physics (Science Paper 1)
front_prompt: State Newton's First Law of Motion.
back_answer: A body continues to be in its state of rest or of uniform motion in a straight line unless an external force is applied on it to change that state.

subject: Physics (Science Paper 1)
front_prompt: What is Inertia?
back_answer: Inertia is the inherent property of a body by virtue of which it resists any change in its state of rest or of uniform motion in a straight line.

subject: Physics (Science Paper 1)
front_prompt: What physical quantity is a direct measure of inertia?
back_answer: Mass. Greater the mass of a body, greater is its inertia and vice versa.

subject: Physics (Science Paper 1)
front_prompt: Define Linear Momentum.
back_answer: Linear momentum of a body is defined as the product of its mass and its velocity. It is a vector quantity represented by $p = m \times v$.

subject: Physics (Science Paper 1)
front_prompt: State the SI unit of linear momentum.
back_answer: Kilogram metre per second ($kg \, m s^{-1}$ or $N s$).

subject: Physics (Science Paper 1)
front_prompt: State Newton's Second Law of Motion.
back_answer: The rate of change of linear momentum of a body is directly proportional to the applied external force and takes place in the direction in which the force acts.

subject: Physics (Science Paper 1)
front_prompt: Derive the relation $F = ma$ from Newton's Second Law.
back_answer: Force $F$ is proportional to rate of change of momentum: $F \propto \frac{mv - mu}{t} = m(\frac{v-u}{t}) = ma$. Choosing the constant of proportionality as 1 gives $F = ma$.

subject: Physics (Science Paper 1)
front_prompt: State Newton's Third Law of Motion.
back_answer: To every action, there is always an equal and opposite reaction.

subject: Physics (Science Paper 1)
front_prompt: State the Law of Conservation of Linear Momentum.
back_answer: If no external force acts on a system of interacting bodies, the total linear momentum of the system remains conserved (constant).

subject: Physics (Science Paper 1)
front_prompt: What is a natural magnet?
back_answer: An ore of iron called magnetite (or lodestone, $Fe_3O_4$) that possesses magnetic properties naturally and is found in the earth.

subject: Physics (Science Paper 1)
front_prompt: State the Law of Magnetic Poles.
back_answer: Like magnetic poles repel each other, whereas unlike magnetic poles attract each other.

subject: Physics (Science Paper 1)
front_prompt: What is magnetic induction?
back_answer: The phenomenon by which a piece of magnetic material acquires temporary magnetism when placed near or in contact with a magnet.

subject: Physics (Science Paper 1)
front_prompt: What is a neutral point in a magnetic field?
back_answer: A point in a magnetic field where the resultant magnetic field is zero because the magnetic field of the magnet is nullified by the earth's horizontal magnetic field.

subject: Physics (Science Paper 1)
front_prompt: What is the Earth's magnetic property used in navigation called?
back_answer: A freely suspended magnet always comes to rest in the approximate geographic North-South direction.

subject: Physics (Science Paper 1)
front_prompt: Name the method used to magnetize a steel bar using two permanent magnets.
back_answer: The Divided Touch Method (or Double Touch Method).

subject: Physics (Science Paper 1)
front_prompt: What is a magnetic field line?
back_answer: An imaginary continuous curve along which a unit North pole would tend to move if free to do so in a magnetic field.

subject: Physics (Science Paper 1)
front_prompt: Why can two magnetic field lines never intersect each other?
back_answer: If they intersected, it would mean there are two directions of the magnetic field at that single point, which is physically impossible.

subject: Physics (Science Paper 1)
front_prompt: What is the purpose of keepers in storing magnets?
back_answer: Keepers are soft iron bars placed across the poles of magnets to prevent self-demagnetization caused by free-pole repulsion and preserve magnetic strength.

subject: Physics (Science Paper 1)
front_prompt: Differentiate between soft iron and steel in terms of retentivity and coercivity.
back_answer: Soft iron has high retentivity and low coercivity (suitable for temporary magnets/electromagnets), whereas steel has low retentivity and high coercivity (suitable for permanent magnets).

subject: Biology (Science Paper 3)
chapter: Population - The Increasing Numbers and Rising Problems
front_prompt: Define Population.
back_answer: The total number of individuals of a particular species living in a specific geographical area at a given time.

subject: Biology (Science Paper 3)
chapter: Population - The Increasing Numbers and Rising Problems
front_prompt: What is Demography?
back_answer: The statistical study of human population, including size, growth, density, distribution, and vital statistics such as births and deaths.

subject: Biology (Science Paper 3)
chapter: Population - The Increasing Numbers and Rising Problems
front_prompt: Define Birth Rate (Natality).
back_answer: The number of live births per 1,000 people of the population per year.

subject: Biology (Science Paper 3)
chapter: Population - The Increasing Numbers and Rising Problems
front_prompt: Define Death Rate (Mortality).
back_answer: The number of deaths per 1,000 people of the population per year.

subject: Biology (Science Paper 3)
chapter: Population - The Increasing Numbers and Rising Problems
front_prompt: What is meant by Population Density?
back_answer: The number of individuals living per unit area (e.g., per square kilometre) at a given time.

subject: Biology (Science Paper 3)
chapter: Population - The Increasing Numbers and Rising Problems
front_prompt: What is meant by 'Growth Rate of Population'?
back_answer: The difference between the birth rate and the death rate, usually expressed as a percentage per year.

subject: Biology (Science Paper 3)
chapter: Population - The Increasing Numbers and Rising Problems
front_prompt: State two major reasons for the rapid rise in human population.
back_answer: 1. Decrease in death rate due to better healthcare and medical facilities. 2. Increase in life expectancy.

subject: Biology (Science Paper 3)
chapter: Population - The Increasing Numbers and Rising Problems
front_prompt: What is meant by Zero Population Growth?
back_answer: A condition where the birth rate equals the death rate, resulting in a stable population size (growth rate is zero).

subject: Biology (Science Paper 3)
chapter: Population - The Increasing Numbers and Rising Problems
front_prompt: List two major problems caused by overpopulation in a country.
back_answer: 1. Scarcity of resources (food, water, energy). 2. Unemployment and severe environmental pollution.

subject: Biology (Science Paper 3)
chapter: Population - The Increasing Numbers and Rising Problems
front_prompt: Define Infant Mortality Rate.
back_answer: The number of deaths of children under one year of age per 1,000 live births in a given year.

subject: History and Civics (H.C.G. Paper 1)
front_prompt: When and where was the Quit India Resolution passed by the All-India Congress Committee?
back_answer: Passed on August 8, 1942, at the Gowalia Tank maidan in Bombay (Mumbai).

subject: History and Civics (H.C.G. Paper 1)
front_prompt: Who gave the famous slogan 'Do or Die' (Karenge ya Marenge) during the Quit India Movement?
back_answer: Mahatma Gandhi.

subject: History and Civics (H.C.G. Paper 1)
front_prompt: What was the immediate cause that led to the launching of the Quit India Movement?
back_answer: The failure of the Cripps Mission in 1942 and growing discontent with British rule amidst the threat of Japanese invasion.

subject: History and Civics (H.C.G. Paper 1)
front_prompt: Name the British Prime Minister who sent the Cripps Mission to India in 1942.
back_answer: Winston Churchill.

subject: History and Civics (H.C.G. Paper 1)
front_prompt: Why was the Cripps Mission rejected by the Indian National Congress and the Muslim League?
back_answer: Because it offered only dominion status after the war and contained provisions for the partition of India (provincial option to stay out of the Indian Union).

subject: History and Civics (H.C.G. Paper 1)
front_prompt: What happened to the top leadership of the Indian National Congress immediately after the Quit India Resolution was passed on August 8, 1942?
back_answer: Early in the morning on August 9, 1942, almost all top leaders including Mahatma Gandhi, Jawaharlal Nehru, and Vallabhbhai Patel were arrested under the Defense of India Rules.

subject: History and Civics (H.C.G. Paper 1)
front_prompt: Name the prominent socialist leader who escaped from Hazaribagh Central Jail and organized underground resistance during the Quit India Movement.
back_answer: Jayaprakash Narayan.

subject: History and Civics (H.C.G. Paper 1)
front_prompt: Who hoisted the Indian National Congress flag at the Gowalia Tank maidan on August 9, 1942, following the arrest of senior leaders?
back_answer: Aruna Asaf Ali.

subject: History and Civics (H.C.G. Paper 1)
front_prompt: What was the significance of parallel governments established during the Quit India Movement? Give one example.
back_answer: They demonstrated the ability of Indians to self-govern; e.g., the 'Prati Sarkar' established in Satara, Maharashtra.

subject: History and Civics (H.C.G. Paper 1)
front_prompt: How did the Quit India Movement mark a major turning point in India's freedom struggle?
back_answer: It was a leaderless, mass uprising characterized by unprecedented spontaneous participation of the common people, demonstrating that the British could no longer rule India without consent.

subject: History and Civics (H.C.G. Paper 1)
front_prompt: When and by whom was the Forward Bloc founded?
back_answer: The Forward Bloc was founded by Subhas Chandra Bose in May 1939 after his resignation from the Congress presidentship.

subject: History and Civics (H.C.G. Paper 1)
front_prompt: What was the main objective of forming the Forward Bloc?
back_answer: To bring together all left-wing sections inside the Congress and consolidate all anti-imperialist forces in the country to fight British imperialism.

subject: History and Civics (H.C.G. Paper 1)
front_prompt: Who originally conceived the idea of the Indian National Army (INA)?
back_answer: Captain Mohan Singh, an officer of the British-Indian Army.

subject: History and Civics (H.C.G. Paper 1)
front_prompt: From which group of people was the INA primarily formed initially?
back_answer: Indian prisoners of war (POWs) captured by the Japanese forces in Southeast Asia.

subject: History and Civics (H.C.G. Paper 1)
front_prompt: Who handed over the leadership of the INA to Subhas Chandra Bose in 1943?
back_answer: Rash Behari Bose

subject: History and Civics (H.C.G. Paper 1)
front_prompt: What was the popular title conferred upon Subhas Chandra Bose by the people?
back_answer: Netaji

subject: History and Civics (H.C.G. Paper 1)
front_prompt: Name the Provisional Government of Free India established by Subhas Chandra Bose in October 1943.
back_answer: Arzi Hukumat-e-Azad Hind

subject: History and Civics (H.C.G. Paper 1)
front_prompt: What were the famous battle cries/slogans given by Subhas Chandra Bose to the INA?
back_answer: 'Jai Hind' and 'Delhi Chalo'

subject: History and Civics (H.C.G. Paper 1)
front_prompt: Name the women's regiment of the INA.
back_answer: The Rani of Jhansi Regiment

subject: History and Civics (H.C.G. Paper 1)
front_prompt: Where were the historic public trials of the INA prisoners held by the British?
back_answer: The Red Fort in Delhi

subject: History and Civics (H.C.G. Paper 1)
front_prompt: Who was the Governor-General of India who announced the Plan for the partition of India on June 3, 1947?
back_answer: Lord Mountbatten

subject: History and Civics (H.C.G. Paper 1)
front_prompt: What was the primary objective of the Cabinet Mission Plan sent to India in 1946?
back_answer: To discuss and plan for the transfer of power from the British government to Indian leadership and set up a constitution-making body.

subject: History and Civics (H.C.G. Paper 1)
front_prompt: Which Muslim League leader proclaimed August 16, 1946, as 'Direct Action Day'?
back_answer: Muhammad Ali Jinnah

subject: History and Civics (H.C.G. Paper 1)
front_prompt: Under the Mountbatten Plan, how was the decision regarding the partition of Punjab and Bengal to be determined?
back_answer: By the vote of the members of the Provincial Legislative Assemblies in respective provinces, divided into Muslim-majority and non-Muslim-majority districts.

subject: History and Civics (H.C.G. Paper 1)
front_prompt: Name the act passed by the British Parliament that formally created the independent dominions of India and Pakistan.
back_answer: The Indian Independence Act of 1947

subject: History and Civics (H.C.G. Paper 1)
front_prompt: When did the Indian Independence Act, 1947, receive royal assent?

subject: History and Civics (H.C.G. Paper 1)
front_prompt: Who headed the boundary commissions appointed under the Mountbatten Plan to demarcate the international borders for Punjab and Bengal?
back_answer: Sir Cyril Radcliffe

subject: History and Civics (H.C.G. Paper 1)
front_prompt: What provision was made in the Indian Independence Act, 1947, regarding the Princely States?
back_answer: Paramountcy of the British Crown lapsed, and Princely States were given the option to accede to either India or Pakistan or remain independent.

subject: History and Civics (H.C.G. Paper 1)
front_prompt: Who became the first Governor-General of independent Pakistan?
back_answer: Muhammad Ali Jinnah

subject: History and Civics (H.C.G. Paper 1)
front_prompt: Who served as the first Governor-General of independent India?
back_answer: Lord Mountbatten

subject: History and Civics (H.C.G. Paper 1)
front_prompt: When did the First World War begin and end?
back_answer: The First World War began on July 28, 1914, and ended on November 11, 1918.

subject: History and Civics (H.C.G. Paper 1)
front_prompt: Name the immediate cause of the First World War.
back_answer: The assassination of Archduke Franz Ferdinand, heir to the Austro-Hungarian throne, and his wife at Sarajevo on June 28, 1914.

subject: History and Civics (H.C.G. Paper 1)
front_prompt: What was the Triple Alliance formed in 1882?
back_answer: A secret military alliance between Germany, Austria-Hungary, and Italy, formed by Bismarck to isolate France.

subject: History and Civics (H.C.G. Paper 1)
front_prompt: Which nations formed the Triple Entente in 1907?
back_answer: Britain, France, and Russia.

subject: History and Civics (H.C.G. Paper 1)
front_prompt: Define Imperialism in the context of the causes of the First World War.
back_answer: The policy of expanding a nation's power and influence through colonization, military force, or economic dominance, which led to intense colonial rivalry among European powers in Asia and Africa.

subject: History and Civics (H.C.G. Paper 1)
front_prompt: What was the significance of the Treaty of Versailles (1919)?
back_answer: It officially ended the state of war between Germany and the Allied Powers, imposed severe territorial and financial penalties on Germany, and established the League of Nations.

subject: History and Civics (H.C.G. Paper 1)
front_prompt: What was the primary objective behind the formation of the League of Nations?
back_answer: To promote international cooperation, achieve international peace and security, and prevent future global conflicts through collective security and disarmament.

subject: History and Civics (H.C.G. Paper 1)
front_prompt: How did Militarism contribute to the outbreak of the First World War?
back_answer: European powers engaged in a massive arms race, stockpiling weapons and expanding their armies and navies, creating an atmosphere of fear, suspicion, and readiness for war.

subject: History and Civics (H.C.G. Paper 1)
front_prompt: Name the two opposing blocs of nations during the First World War.
back_answer: The Allied Powers (Britain, France, Russia, Italy, Japan, and later the USA) and the Central Powers (Germany, Austria-Hungary, Ottoman Empire, and Bulgaria).

subject: History and Civics (H.C.G. Paper 1)
front_prompt: What was the 'War Guilt Clause' in the Treaty of Versailles?
back_answer: Article 231 of the treaty, which forced Germany to accept sole responsibility for causing all the loss and damage of the war.

subject: History and Civics (H.C.G. Paper 1)
front_prompt: What was the primary political ideology behind Benito Mussolini's rule in Italy?
back_answer: Fascism

subject: History and Civics (H.C.G. Paper 1)
front_prompt: Name the paramilitary volunteer organization formed by Benito Mussolini in Italy known for wearing black shirts.
back_answer: The Blackshirts (Squadristi)

subject: History and Civics (H.C.G. Paper 1)
front_prompt: When did Mussolini and his Fascist followers march on Rome to seize political power?
back_answer: October 1922

subject: History and Civics (H.C.G. Paper 1)
front_prompt: What was the official title assumed by Benito Mussolini as the supreme dictator of Italy?
back_answer: Il Duce (The Leader)

subject: History and Civics (H.C.G. Paper 1)
front_prompt: What was the full name of the political party led by Adolf Hitler in Germany?
back_answer: National Socialist German Workers' Party (Nazi Party)

subject: History and Civics (H.C.G. Paper 1)
front_prompt: Name the autobiography written by Adolf Hitler during his imprisonment after the Munich Putsch.
back_answer: Mein Kampf (My Struggle)

subject: History and Civics (H.C.G. Paper 1)
front_prompt: What was the name of the paramilitary wing of the Nazi Party, distinguished by their brown uniforms?
back_answer: The Brownshirts (Sturmabteilung or SA)

subject: History and Civics (H.C.G. Paper 1)
front_prompt: When was Adolf Hitler appointed as the Chancellor of Germany?
back_answer: January 30, 1933

subject: History and Civics (H.C.G. Paper 1)
front_prompt: What title did Adolf Hitler assume after the death of President Paul von Hindenburg, combining the offices of Chancellor and President?
back_answer: Der Führer (The Leader)

subject: History and Civics (H.C.G. Paper 1)
front_prompt: Mention one major socio-economic factor that contributed significantly to the rise of dictatorships in Europe after World War I.
back_answer: Economic devastation, massive unemployment, and hyperinflation caused by the Great Depression and the costs of World War I.

subject: History and Civics (H.C.G. Paper 1)
front_prompt: When did the Second World War officially begin and end?
back_answer: It began on September 1, 1939 (with Germany's invasion of Poland) and ended on September 2, 1945.

subject: History and Civics (H.C.G. Paper 1)
front_prompt: Name the two major rival military alliances that fought in the Second World War.
back_answer: The Axis Powers (Germany, Italy, Japan) and the Allied Powers (Britain, France, Soviet Union, USA, China, etc.).

subject: History and Civics (H.C.G. Paper 1)
front_prompt: What immediate event caused Great Britain and France to declare war on Germany on September 3, 1939?
back_answer: Germany's unprovoked invasion of Poland on September 1, 1939.

subject: History and Civics (H.C.G. Paper 1)
front_prompt: What was the policy of Appeasement pursued by Britain and France towards Nazi Germany?
back_answer: A diplomatic strategy of making concessions to aggressive powers (like Hitler) to maintain peace and avoid a major European war.

subject: History and Civics (H.C.G. Paper 1)
front_prompt: State the significance of the attack on Pearl Harbor.
back_answer: On December 7, 1941, Japan attacked the US naval base at Pearl Harbor, prompting the United States to formally enter the Second World War.

subject: History and Civics (H.C.G. Paper 1)
front_prompt: What was the Hitler-Stalin Pact (Nazi-Soviet Non-Aggression Pact) of August 1939?
back_answer: A non-aggression treaty between Germany and the Soviet Union agreeing not to attack each other and secretly dividing Eastern Europe into spheres of influence.

subject: History and Civics (H.C.G. Paper 1)
front_prompt: What were the atomic bombings that led to the surrender of Japan in August 1945?
